entries.reviewSummary: Sets incorporator standards and classes of insurance, minimum capital and surplus thresholds for stock and mutual companies, and statutory phase-in schedules.

headings.title: Formation of insurance corporations and authorized classes
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes thirteen or more persons to incorporate for property, liability, fidelity, surety, accident, health, and miscellaneous insurance classes.

headings.title: Minimum capital and surplus requirements by class
headings.reviewNote: Establishes minimum paid-in capital and surplus for stock insurers and policyholders' surplus for mutual insurers transacting one or multiple insurance classes.

headings.title: Certificate revocation for statutory violations
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that violation of section provisions constitutes grounds for revocation of the insurer's certificate of authority by the director.

headings.title: Phase-in schedule for mutual insurer surplus
headings.reviewNote: Provides a multi-year phase-in schedule through 1992 for mutual insurers licensed as of July 1, 1987, to meet minimum policyholders' surplus levels.

headings.title: Phase-in schedule for stock insurer capital and surplus
headings.reviewNote: Sets a multi-year phase-in schedule through December 31, 1992, for stock insurers licensed on August 28, 1989 (multiple classes) or July 1, 1987 (one class) to reach required capital and surplus minimums.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes electronic delivery of insurance notices and documents, outlining consent, verification, withdrawal, paper cost protections, and statutory scope.

headings.title: Definitions for electronic insurance document delivery
headings.reviewNote: Defines delivered by electronic means and party for insurance transaction communications.

headings.title: Legal validity of electronic notices and documents
headings.reviewNote: Permits electronic delivery, storage, and presentation of insurance notices and documents meeting sections 432.200 to 432.295 (subject to subsection 3), making such delivery equivalent to required mail methods.

headings.title: Conditions for electronic delivery and consent
headings.reviewNote: Details conditions for electronic delivery including affirmative consent, disclosure of rights and hardware requirements, and withdrawal mechanisms.

headings.title: Presumption of consent for direct web purchases
headings.reviewNote: Presumes electronic delivery consent for insurance policies purchased directly online while preserving the party's right of withdrawal.

headings.title: Notice timing content and verification requirements
headings.reviewNote: Preserves statutory notice timing and content rules, requires delivery verification where mandated, and regulates contract validity conditions.

headings.title: Effective date and effect of consent withdrawal
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that withdrawal of electronic consent takes effect within thirty days and does not affect prior electronic deliveries.

headings.title: Prior electronic consent and supplemental notifications
headings.reviewNote: Governs pre-August 28, 2013 electronic consents and requires prior notice of additional documents and withdrawal rights before expansion.

headings.title: Prohibition of fees for paper document delivery
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits charging additional fees or costs to parties who refuse electronic delivery or withdraw their consent.

headings.title: Satisfaction of notarization and verification requirements
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes electronic signatures to satisfy notarization, acknowledgment, verification, or oath requirements when logically associated with documents.

headings.title: Construction with other laws and chapter scope
headings.reviewNote: Preserves sections 354.442, 376.1450, and 432.200 to 432.295, and applies the section to chapter 379 and chapter 380 insurers and to life insurance product notices and documents issued by chapter 376 insurers.

headings.title: Premium discounts for electronic document election
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that insurers may offer discounts to insureds who elect to receive notices and documents electronically.

entries.reviewSummary: Allows electronic posting of standard insurance policies and endorsements on insurer websites subject to retention, notice, and rulemaking standards.

headings.title: Website posting of policy forms and endorsements
headings.reviewNote: Permits insurers, including chapter 380 insurers, to post policy forms and endorsements for section 379.010(1)(1), (2), (3), and (5) lines on their website in lieu of paper delivery if they contain no personally identifiable information.

headings.title: Conditions for website posting of policy forms
headings.reviewNote: Establishes conditions for website posting including retention of expired forms, accessibility, clear notice on declarations pages, and paper copies upon request.

headings.title: Promulgation of rules by insurance director
headings.reviewNote: Grants rulemaking authority to the director to administer online posting of policy forms under chapter 536 procedures.

entries.reviewSummary: Outlines authorized investments for capital, surplus, and assets of stock and mutual insurers and provides regulatory revocation penalties for violations.

headings.title: Authorized investments for capital surplus and assets
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates permitted investments for minimum capital and remaining surplus or assets of stock and mutual companies, including government obligations, corporate debt, real estate, and investment pools.

headings.title: Penalties for violation of investment limitations
headings.reviewNote: Makes violation of investment provisions grounds for suspension or revocation of an insurer's certificate of authority.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates asset maintenance for domestic property and liability insurers, detailing policyholder obligation definitions and quantitative diversification limits.

headings.title: Asset diversification and liquidity requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires domestic property and liability insurers to maintain diversified and reasonably liquid assets to cover policyholder obligations.

headings.title: Definitions of insurer and policyholder obligations
headings.reviewNote: Defines domestic insurer and policyholder obligations, including unearned premium and claim reserves, minimum capital, and reinsurance balances.

headings.title: Diversification standards for policyholder obligations
headings.reviewNote: Establishes quantitative caps and qualification rules for investments covering policyholder obligations across securities, real estate, and subsidiaries; source note indicates word 'an' appears before 'investments' in original rolls.

headings.title: Standard for determining reasonable asset liquidity
headings.reviewNote: Defines reasonably liquid assets as those convertible to cash within a reasonable time to discharge insurer liabilities.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes insurer participation in qualified investment pools, establishing asset limits, manager standards, custodial agreements, and regulatory reporting rules.

headings.title: Definitions for insurer investment pool participation
headings.reviewNote: Defines affiliate, business entity, and qualified bank for purposes of insurer investment pool regulations.

headings.title: Authorized pool investments and maximum pool participation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes investment in qualified pools holding eligible assets, limits proportionate interest to statutory caps, and caps participation at three pools.

headings.title: Prohibited investments and transactions for investment pools
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits investment pools from acquiring participant securities, incurring unauthorized debt, lending to participants, or exceeding single-entity caps.

headings.title: Aggregate investment limits for investment pools
headings.reviewNote: Restricts pool investments to ten percent of admitted assets in a single pool and thirty percent across all investment pools.

headings.title: Pool manager qualifications and custody account requirements
headings.reviewNote: Sets qualifications for pool managers, detailed accounting mandates, and requirements for custody accounts and agreements with qualified banks.

headings.title: Mandatory provisions for written pooling agreements
headings.reviewNote: Establishes required written pooling agreement terms, including 100% insurer/affiliate ownership, non-commingling, undivided pro rata interests, insolvency withdrawal rights, penalty-free demand withdrawals settled within five business days, and director record inspection.

headings.title: Business entity status of investment pool
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an investment pool authorized pursuant to this section shall be a business entity.

headings.title: Prior approval of pooling agreements and annual reporting
headings.reviewNote: Requires prior department approval of pooling agreements and amendments under section 382.195, exempts ordinary-course pool transactions from section 382.195, and requires annual reporting under section 382.100.

entries.reviewSummary: Prescribes minimum guaranty fund surplus, applicant agreements, and cash premium thresholds for mutual fire and marine insurers with phase-in relief and revocation sanctions.

headings.title: Minimum surplus and applicant requirements for mutuals
headings.reviewNote: Requires mutual fire and marine companies to maintain $1.6 million surplus and agreements with 200 applicants totaling $100,000 paid cash premiums.

headings.title: Temporary phase-in exception for existing mutual insurers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a phase-in period through December 31, 1989, for existing licensed mutual companies to meet the full $1.6 million surplus requirement.

headings.title: Certificate revocation for violation of mutual standards
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to revoke the certificate of authority of any mutual insurer violating section provisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates the issuance, deposit, cash payment, assessment, and property lien security of premium notes given to mutual insurance companies.

headings.title: Deposit and assessment terms of premium notes
headings.reviewNote: Requires deposit of a premium note with minimum ten percent cash down payment, subject to board assessment for losses and expenses.

headings.title: Lien on insured property securing premium note
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a lien on insured buildings and other real and personal property, together with the insured's interest in the underlying land, to secure the premium note upon written assent on its face.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs the assessment process, proportional formulas, publication notices, enforcement actions, and maximum liability limits for mutual premium notes.

headings.title: Board authority to assess premium notes
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the board of directors of a mutual company to assess premium notes to settle losses, expenses, and liabilities.

headings.title: Proportional calculation of premium note assessments
headings.reviewNote: Directs assessments to be made proportionally on all notes in existence for one year based on note face amounts.

headings.title: Payment due date and notice requirements
headings.reviewNote: Makes assessments due within thirty days after newspaper publication and written notice to the maker, requiring endorsement of payment on the note.

headings.title: Mandatory contents of newspaper assessment notice
headings.reviewNote: Specifies required information in the published assessment notice, including aggregate note values, losses, claimants, expenses, and cash on hand.

headings.title: Legal action for recovery of delinquent notes
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes directors to sue for and recover the entire amount of the premium note with costs if an assessment remains unpaid for thirty days.

headings.title: Maximum liability limit on premium notes
headings.reviewNote: Limits a person's aggregate liability on a premium note to the face amount of the note.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates annual sworn financial reports for property and casualty insurers detailing assets and liabilities, while protecting officer compensation from public disclosure.

headings.title: Annual financial statement filing and required contents
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual sworn financial statements from property and casualty insurers detailing capital, assets, liabilities, risks, and receipts.

headings.title: Confidentiality of employee and officer compensation data
headings.reviewNote: Exempts employee and officer compensation information in filed annual statements from public disclosure outside the insurance department.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates property and casualty certificates of insurance, establishing filing mandates, disclaimer wording, prohibited representations, producer fees, and enforcement powers.

headings.title: Definitions for certificates of insurance regulation
headings.reviewNote: Defines certificate holder, certificate of insurance, director, insurance producer, insurer, person, and policyholder.

headings.title: Filing requirement for certificate of insurance forms
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits preparing, issuing, or requesting unfiled certificate forms or altering filed certificate of insurance forms.

headings.title: Mandatory informational disclaimer statement on certificates
headings.reviewNote: Requires certificates of insurance to contain a statement that the certificate is for information only and does not alter policy coverage.

headings.title: Compliance status of ACORD and ISO standard forms
headings.reviewNote: Deems standard certificate forms promulgated by ACORD or ISO compliant upon filing with the director for use by members.

headings.title: Prohibition against requesting false or misleading certificates
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits requesting or demanding a certificate of insurance containing false or misleading information about the underlying policy.

headings.title: Prohibition against issuing false or misleading certificates
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits knowingly issuing a certificate containing false information or purporting to alter or extend policy coverage.

headings.title: Restrictions on opinion letters and addenda
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits issuing opinion letters inconsistent with statute while permitting compliant endorsement listing addenda.

headings.title: Statewide applicability of certificate of insurance rules
headings.reviewNote: Applies statutory certificate provisions to all certificate holders, policyholders, insurers, and producers covering Missouri risks.

headings.title: Legal status of certificate and holder rights
headings.reviewNote: Declares a certificate is not an insurance policy and confers no rights beyond those expressly granted in the underlying policy.

headings.title: Prohibition of contract references or opinions on certificates
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits certificate references or opinions regarding the effect of underlying construction or service contracts.

headings.title: Notice rights limited to policy terms and endorsements
headings.reviewNote: Limits a certificate holder's right to notice of cancellation or nonrenewal to rights expressly provided in the policy or endorsements.

headings.title: Service fee authorization for insurance producers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes insurance producers to charge a reasonable service fee for issuing a certificate of insurance to an insured or holder.

headings.title: Unenforceability of noncompliant certificate forms and documents
headings.reviewNote: Declares void and unenforceable any certificate, document, or correspondence prepared, issued, or requested in violation of this section.

headings.title: Administrative enforcement orders and penalties by director
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to issue cease and desist orders, civil penalties, and other administrative remedies for violations.

headings.title: Investigative and examination powers of insurance director
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the director to examine and investigate any person reasonably believed to be violating certificate of insurance statutes.

headings.title: Promulgation of rules for certificate administration
headings.reviewNote: Grants the director authority to adopt administrative rules to implement certificate of insurance provisions under chapter 536.

headings.title: Producer immunity for unapproved commercial property evidence
headings.reviewNote: Bars lender causes of action against an insurance producer arising from use of an exempted unapproved evidence of commercial property insurance form when advised in writing, except for intentional misrepresentation or fraud.

entries.reviewSummary: Delineates exclusive permissible grounds for cancelling automobile policies, preserves unknown pre-renewal cancellation grounds, and prohibits discriminatory underwriting or prior-cancellation inquiries for experienced drivers.

headings.title: Permissible statutory grounds for policy cancellation
headings.reviewNote: Restricts automobile policy cancellations to nonpayment of premium or suspension or revocation of the named insured's driver's license, permitting a named-driver exclusion instead of cancellation when multiple insureds are named.

headings.title: Non-waiver of pre-existing cancellation grounds upon renewal
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that policy renewal does not waive or estop grounds for cancellation that existed before the effective renewal date and were unknown to the insurer at renewal.

headings.title: Prohibited underwriting grounds for experienced drivers
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits cancelling, refusing to write, or refusing to renew auto insurance for drivers with at least two years' experience based solely on protected traits, lawful occupation including military service, or prior insurer refusal/cancellation, and bars requiring disclosure of prior cancellations, subject to class and territory provisos.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes timing and delivery procedures for automobile cancellation, renewal, and coverage reduction notices, authorizing reinstatement and affiliate transfer exemptions.

headings.title: Mandatory advance notice of cancellation or nonrenewal
headings.reviewNote: Requires thirty days' written notice of cancellation or nonrenewal, or ten days' notice for nonpayment, specifying required contents.

headings.title: Unequivocal legal effect of cancellation notice
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that issuance of a cancellation notice constitutes a present and unequivocal act of cancellation.

headings.title: Discretionary policy reinstatement and notice validity
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes insurers to reinstate cancelled policies without invalidating the legal effectiveness of the original cancellation notice.

headings.title: Renewal notice requirements and coverage reduction notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires fifteen days' advance written or electronic notice for automobile policy renewals and proposed coverage reductions.

headings.title: Exemption for inter-affiliate policy transfers
headings.reviewNote: Exempts insurers transferring policies between holding company affiliates from nonrenewal notice requirements if statutory replacement notices are given.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates thirty-day written explanations with specific factual grounds when automobile insurance is refused, exempting placements with corporate affiliates.

headings.title: Mandatory written explanation of automobile refusal
headings.reviewNote: Requires written explanation within thirty days of refusing automobile insurance, detailing specific reasons and assigned risk plan availability.

headings.title: Affiliate placement exemption from explanation requirement
headings.reviewNote: Exempts insurers from sending a written refusal explanation if the applicant is written on a policy by an affiliated company.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits auto insurance discrimination based on lack of prior coverage caused by military service, preserves driving record evaluations, and mandates service member notice.

headings.title: Adverse underwriting bar for first-time military applicants
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits adverse underwriting decisions against military members who have never purchased motor vehicle insurance due to active service.

headings.title: Adverse underwriting bar for prior military coverage lapses
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits adverse underwriting decisions based on lack of prior insurance during military service, while allowing discounts for continuous coverage.

headings.title: Permissible consideration of applicant driving record
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that insurers may base adverse underwriting decisions on substandard driving records rather than military coverage gaps.

headings.title: Verification proof of military service eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes insurers to require reasonable proof of military service and eligibility under the section.

headings.title: Adjutant general notice to military members
headings.reviewNote: Directs the state adjutant general to notify military personnel of motor vehicle insurance protections and encourages federal notification.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits assigning fault in insurance claims based solely on lawful motorcycle operation, designating violations as unfair trade practices.

headings.title: Prohibition of motorcycle fault attribution
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits assigning fault in accident investigations or insurance claims based solely on legal operation of a motorcycle.

headings.title: Unfair trade practice classification and penalties
headings.reviewNote: Classifies violation of motorcycle fault prohibitions as an unfair trade practice subject to chapter 375 statutory penalties.

headings.title: Definitions of insurer and automobile policy
headings.reviewNote: Defines insurer and automobile insurance policy covering private passenger automobiles owned by individuals or partnerships.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs licensing, permitted insurance lines, operational prerequisites, and application filings for Missouri captive insurance companies.

headings.title: Permitted and restricted captive insurance lines
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes captive insurers to write property, casualty, life, and accident lines while restricting pure, association, and industrial risks.

headings.title: In-state business operational and licensing requirements
headings.reviewNote: Conditions captive insurer operations on licensing, annual in-state board meetings, Missouri principal place of business, and registered agent appointment.

headings.title: Application documentation and review standards
headings.reviewNote: Specifies license application filings (organizational documents, sworn financial statement, coverage/rate descriptions, liquidity/management/loss-prevention evidence), confidentiality and disclosure exceptions, $7,500 license and annual renewal fees, and license issuance until April first.

entries.reviewSummary: Sets minimum capital and surplus thresholds by captive type, authorizing director adjustments and letters of credit.

headings.title: Minimum paid-in capital and surplus thresholds
headings.reviewNote: Establishes minimum capital and surplus thresholds of $250,000 for pure captives and $500,000 for association, industrial, and sponsored captives.

headings.title: Discretionary additional capital and surplus requirements
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to require additional capital and surplus based on volume, nature, and types of insurance written.

headings.title: Permissible forms of capital and surplus
headings.reviewNote: Permits capital and surplus to be held in cash or an approved irrevocable letter of credit issued by a qualifying bank.

entries.reviewSummary: Details organizational structures, incorporator standards, general good findings, board composition, and merger procedures for captive insurers.

headings.title: Authorized corporate forms for pure captives
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes pure captive insurers to organize as stock corporations, nonprofit corporations, or manager-managed limited liability companies.

headings.title: Organizational forms for association and industrial captives
headings.reviewNote: Allows association and industrial captives to form as stock corporations, mutual insurers, manager-managed limited liability companies, or reciprocals.

headings.title: Minimum incorporator and residency requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires at least three incorporators or organizers for captive insurers, with at least one being a Missouri resident.

headings.title: Director petition and public interest findings
headings.reviewNote: Mandates director certification that the captive insurer will promote the general good of the state before corporate filings.

headings.title: Issuance of capital stock without par value
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes stock captive insurance companies to issue shares with no par value.

headings.title: Missouri residency requirement for governing body
headings.reviewNote: Requires at least one Missouri resident on the board of directors of a corporate captive, among the managers of an LLC captive, or on the subscribers' advisory committee of a reciprocal captive.

headings.title: Application of general corporation and insurance law
headings.reviewNote: Applies general corporation and insurance statutes to corporate captives where not inconsistent with captive insurance provisions.

headings.title: Application of LLC and nonprofit corporation statutes
headings.reviewNote: Applies chapter 347 to LLC captives and chapter 355 to nonprofit corporation captives, with sections 379.1300 to 379.1351 controlling in the event of conflict.

headings.title: Mergers consolidations conversions and redomestications
headings.reviewNote: Governs mergers, consolidations, redomestications, and mutual holding company conversions involving captive insurance companies.

headings.title: Quorum requirements for corporate boards of directors
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes corporate captive bylaws to establish board quorums of not less than one-third of directors, with a two-director minimum.

headings.title: Applicable laws for reciprocal captive insurers
headings.reviewNote: Governs reciprocal captive insurers under reciprocal statutes, providing that captive insurance provisions control in case of conflict.

headings.title: Quorum rules for reciprocal advisory committees
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes reciprocal captive organizing documents to set subscriber advisory committee quorums at no fewer than one-third of members.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates annual financial condition reports for captive insurers, establishing filing deadlines, accounting options, and fiscal year alternatives.

headings.title: Exemption from general annual reporting statutes
headings.reviewNote: Exempts captive insurance companies from general insurer annual reporting laws except as specifically provided in captive statutes.

headings.title: Financial condition report filing and accounting standards
headings.reviewNote: Requires captive insurers to submit annual sworn financial reports by March first using GAAP or approved statutory accounting principles.

headings.title: Fiscal year reporting option and statements
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes pure and industrial captives to file annual reports on a fiscal year end with interim calendar year financial statements.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs triennial or quinquennial examinations of captive insurers, assessment of examination expenses, and strict confidentiality protections for work papers.

headings.title: Periodic examinations and expense reimbursement warrants
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to examine captive insurers at least once every three or five years, with examination expenses assessed to the insurer.

headings.title: Application of statutory financial examination procedures
headings.reviewNote: Applies sections 374.202 to 374.207 financial examination standards and procedures to captive insurer examinations.

headings.title: Confidentiality of examination work papers and reports
headings.reviewNote: Declares examination reports, work papers, and related documents confidential and privileged, exempt from subpoena or public disclosure without consent.

entries.reviewSummary: Specifies statutory grounds and administrative authority for the director to suspend or revoke captive insurance company licenses.

headings.title: Statutory grounds for license suspension or revocation
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates grounds for captive license suspension or revocation, including insolvency, report noncompliance, charter breaches, and unsound operations.

headings.title: Discretionary license suspension or revocation authority
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to suspend or revoke a captive insurer's license upon violation when deemed in the public or policyholder interest.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates investments and valuation for association captives, exempts pure and industrial captives subject to solvency limits, and requires director approval for pure captive loans or investments in parents or affiliates.

headings.title: Investment rules for association captive insurance companies
headings.reviewNote: Requires association captives to comply with chapter 375 and sections 379.080 and 379.082 investment laws and NAIC valuation procedures, while allowing director approval of alternative reliable valuation and rating methods.

headings.title: Investment rules for pure and industrial captives
headings.reviewNote: Exempts pure and industrial insured captives from restrictions on allowable investments, provided the director may prohibit or limit any investment threatening solvency or liquidity.

headings.title: Approval for pure captive loans to parents or affiliates
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits a pure captive insurance company from making a loan to or investment in its parent company or affiliates without prior written approval and approved documentation from the director.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs captive reinsurance powers, credit for ceded risks, treatment of qualified self-insured workers' compensation, and pool participation.

headings.title: Authority to provide reinsurance on ceded risks
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes captive insurers to provide reinsurance on property, casualty, and life risks ceded by other authorized insurers.

headings.title: Credit for reinsurance ceded to qualified reinsurers
headings.reviewNote: Governs credit for reinsurance ceded by captive insurers and requires director prior approval for noncompliant reinsurers.

headings.title: Reinsurance treatment of qualified self-insured workers plans
headings.reviewNote: Deems captive insurance of parent or affiliate qualified self-insured workers' compensation plans to be reinsurance.

headings.title: Reinsurance credit for authorized pools and exchanges
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes credit for reinsurance ceded to approved reinsurance pools or exchanges subject to director security standards.

entries.reviewSummary: Imposes tiered premium taxes on direct and assumed captive premiums, setting minimum and maximum caps, local tax exemptions, and fee deductions.

headings.title: Premium tax rates on direct written premiums
headings.reviewNote: Imposes tiered annual premium taxes payable by May first on direct written premiums ranging from 0.38 percent to 0.072 percent after return-premium deductions, excluding annuity contract considerations.

headings.title: Premium tax rates on assumed reinsurance premiums
headings.reviewNote: Imposes tiered annual premium taxes payable by May first on assumed reinsurance premiums ranging from 0.214 percent to 0.024 percent, exempting risks taxed directly and certain common-control discontinuance reserve assumptions.

headings.title: Minimum and maximum annual premium tax limits
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a $7,500 minimum annual premium tax and a $200,000 maximum tax, detailing sponsored captive and protected cell rules.

headings.title: Annual tax return filing and assessment process
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual tax returns by February first, director certification by March thirty-first, and subsequent assessment by the director of revenue.

headings.title: Penalties for delinquent returns and tax payments
headings.reviewNote: Subjects captive insurance companies failing to file required returns or pay assessed taxes on time to sections 148.375 and 148.410.

headings.title: Unitary tax treatment for common control captives
headings.reviewNote: Taxes two or more captive insurers under common ownership and control as a single consolidated captive insurance company.

headings.title: Definitions of common ownership and control
headings.reviewNote: Defines common ownership and control, ownership percentages, and separate protected cell tax treatment under specific conditions.

headings.title: Preemption of local taxes and ad valorem exception
headings.reviewNote: Declares state captive premium taxes in lieu of all other state and local taxes, except local ad valorem property taxes.

headings.title: Allocation of tax revenues to dedicated fund
headings.reviewNote: Allocates ten percent of captive tax receipts to the insurance dedicated fund, subject to a three percent cap, with the rest to general revenue.

headings.title: Annual calculation and proration of multiyear policies
headings.reviewNote: Directs annual calculation of captive premium taxes with mandatory proration of multiyear policies or reinsurance contracts.

headings.title: Deduction and carryforward of licensing fees
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes deduction of captive licensing and renewal fees from premium taxes, allowing up to five years of nonrefundable carryforward.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs captive fees and taxes into the insurance dedicated fund for program administration and promotion, authorizing anticipated warrants.

headings.title: Funding and authorized disbursements for captive regulation
headings.reviewNote: Directs captive fees and taxes into the insurance dedicated fund for regulatory administration and reasonable industry promotion expenses.

headings.title: Anticipation of receipts and warrant issuance authority
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to anticipate dedicated insurance fund receipts and issue administrative expenditure warrants accordingly.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes procedures, equity protections, hearings, director approval, and legal succession for converting captive corporations into reciprocals.

headings.title: Conversion of stock or mutual captive to reciprocal
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes association and industrial captive stock or mutual corporations to convert or merge into reciprocal insurers under an approved plan.

headings.title: Mandatory fair and equitable conversion plan provisions
headings.reviewNote: Requires conversion plans to provide fair terms for retiring ownership interests and protecting dissenting stockholders and policyholders.

headings.title: Director approval standards and plan conversion conditions
headings.reviewNote: Outlines conditions for director approval, including notice, hearings, equitable subscriber interest allocations, and voting approvals.

headings.title: Merger procedures and reciprocal governance equivalents
headings.reviewNote: Governs board-adopted and director-authorized mergers into reciprocal insurers, equating subscribers' advisory committees to boards and subscribers to mutual policyholders, requiring general-good approval and secretary of state filing, allowing surplus-free facilitating reciprocals, and permitting alien insurer parties.

headings.title: Legal effects of conversion or merger on rights and liabilities
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that a conversion or merger results in a single insurer that automatically succeeds to all property, rights, franchises, and liabilities without impairing pending actions, creditor rights, or existing property liens.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes branch captive insurers for ERISA employee benefit plans, requiring maintenance of a Missouri principal place of business.

headings.title: Branch captive establishment and ERISA benefit coverage
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes establishment of branch captives to write insurance and reinsurance for parent employee benefits subject to ERISA.

headings.title: Principal place of business requirement in Missouri
headings.reviewNote: Requires branch captive insurers to maintain the principal place of business for their branch operations within this state.

entries.reviewSummary: Restricts branch captive examinations to branch activities upon proof of home compliance, requiring foreign examination consent.

headings.title: Scope of branch captive operational examinations
headings.reviewNote: Limits branch captive examinations to branch operations if annual foreign certificates of compliance and financial soundness are provided.

headings.title: Examination authority over alien captive home jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Requires alien captive insurers to grant director examination authority in their home forming jurisdiction as a condition of licensure.

entries.reviewSummary: Vests paid property damage title in insurers, invalidates post-loss benefit assignments to repairers as void, and preserves direct payment authorizations.

headings.title: Vesting of legal title upon claim payment
headings.reviewNote: Vests legal title to paid portions of property damage claims in the insurer without requiring assignment, while claimant retains unpaid portions.

headings.title: Prohibition on pre-loss or post-loss policy assignments
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits insureds from assigning policy duties, rights, benefits, or insurer obligations before or after property damage losses.

headings.title: Definition of property insurance assignment agreement
headings.reviewNote: Defines assignment agreement as instruments transferring post-loss property benefits or action rights to service providers or repair contractors.

headings.title: Void status of post-loss assignment agreements
headings.reviewNote: Declares post-loss benefit assignments null and void against public policy, exempting financial institutions, subsequent buyers, and section 537.065 agreements.

headings.title: Penalty classification for assignment agreement violations
headings.reviewNote: Designates solicitation or acceptance of unlawful post-loss property claim assignments as a level two violation under section 374.049.

headings.title: Unenforceability of contracts violating assignment restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Declares void and unenforceable any contract entered into in violation of statutory post-loss property insurance assignment prohibitions.

headings.title: Direct payment authority to service providers permitted
headings.reviewNote: Preserves policyholder authority to direct payments to service providers and requires direct insurer payment when agreed, subject to applicable liens; source notes record original-rolls wording differences ('that' in H.B. 2636 and 'an' in S.B. 835 & 1111, 2026).

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes sponsored captive insurance companies and protected cells, defining structures, participant rules, and asset segregation.

headings.title: Formation of sponsored captive insurance companies
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes one or more sponsors to form sponsored captives as stock, mutual, nonprofit, or manager-managed LLC entities.

headings.title: Definitions for sponsored captive insurance companies
headings.reviewNote: Defines incorporated protected cell, participant, participant contract, protected cell, sponsor, and sponsored captive insurance company.

headings.title: Additional application filing requirements for sponsored captives
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing accounting plans, inspection statements, participant contracts, and fair expense allocation formulas with the director.

headings.title: Conditions for establishing and maintaining protected cells
headings.reviewNote: Sets thirteen conditions for protected cells including participant/sponsor shareholder limits, separate accounting, asset segregation, transfer and dividend approvals, plan-of-operation attributions, annual reports, ten-day insolvency notice, guaranty fund disclaimers, fronting/reinsurance/security options, and separation of solvent cells.

headings.title: Formation of incorporated protected cells
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes establishing a protected cell as a separate chapter 351 corporation or chapter 347 LLC with required articles references and attached prior director approval, without limiting rights of unincorporated cells.

headings.title: Sponsor qualification standards and RRG prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Allows any person approved by the director based on entity structure, financial experience, stability, and reputation to serve as sponsor, while barring risk retention groups from being sponsors or participants.

headings.title: Participant eligibility and risk limitation rules
headings.reviewNote: Permits associations, corporations, LLCs, partnerships, trusts, other business entities, and sponsors to be participants without requiring share ownership or affiliation, and limits participants to insuring only their own risks.

headings.title: Combined cell investments and statutory investment rules
headings.reviewNote: Allows combining assets of two or more protected cells for investment without defeating segregation, requires compliance with sections 379.080 and 379.082 subject to reinsurance-credit or director waivers, and permits approved accounting and alternative valuation methods.

headings.title: Supervision rehabilitation and liquidation of sponsored captives
headings.reviewNote: Applies sections 375.1150 to 375.1246 to sponsored captives while barring use of protected cell assets for non-cell expenses or claims and keeping company capital and surplus available for company claims.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs SPLRC license applications, permitted ceding and hedging powers, Missouri operational prerequisites, sixty-day review deadlines, annual renewals, application fees, and outside consultant billing.

headings.title: SPLRC license application authority
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a SPLRC, when permitted by its organizational documents, to apply to the director for a license to conduct reinsurance in Missouri under sections 379.1353 to 379.1421.

headings.title: Limitation on ceding companies reinsured by SPLRC
headings.reviewNote: Restricts a SPLRC to reinsuring risks of its ceding company, or multiple ceding companies provided all ceding companies are affiliated with one another.

headings.title: Authority to cede assumed risks
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a SPLRC to cede all or a portion of its assumed risks under ceded reinsurance agreements.

headings.title: Risk mitigation through hedges and swaps
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a SPLRC to mitigate risks by purchasing or participating in hedges such as credit default swaps and total return swaps.

headings.title: Requirements for SPLRC to transact business in Missouri
headings.reviewNote: Requires a SPLRC to obtain a license, hold an annual Missouri board meeting, maintain a Missouri principal place of business, appoint a resident registered agent, hold $250,000 minimum cash surplus in Missouri (source note: word 'and' appears in original rolls), and pay fees.

headings.title: SPLRC license application contents and regulatory filings
headings.reviewNote: Specifies required license application documents (organizational docs, sworn financial statement, asset evidence, NAIC biographical sketches, plan of operation, compliance affidavit, investment strategy, capital source), Missouri surplus proof, and ceding-company domiciliary filings and responses.

headings.title: Exclusivity of requirements and plan revision authority
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits imposing other business-transaction requirements on a SPLRC, except the director may require revisions to and compliance with the plan of operation under section 379.1361.

headings.title: Sixty-day department action deadline on complete applications
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to act on a complete application within sixty days provided subdivisions (2) to (4) of subsection 6 are met five days before the deadline, with an officer-certification alternative if domiciliary filings are not required.

headings.title: Annual license term and discretionary renewal
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a granted SPLRC license continues until March first of each year, when it may be renewed at the director's discretion.

headings.title: Nonrefundable application fee and premium tax credit
headings.reviewNote: Requires a $10,000 nonrefundable application fee upon filing, creditable against taxes payable under section 379.1412 notwithstanding its annual aggregate minimum tax.

headings.title: Outside professional review expenses billed to applicant
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to retain outside legal, financial, and actuarial experts at the applicant's expense.

entries.reviewSummary: Specifies mandatory administrative findings, management character standards, and foreign regulatory approvals for licensing an SPLRC.

headings.title: Required findings by director for license issuance
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to find that the plan provides expected successful operation, statutory compliance, and domiciliary state approvals.

headings.title: Evaluation of character and management integrity
headings.reviewNote: Directs consideration of management character and freedom from improper asset manipulation, exempting unrequired foreign approvals.

entries.reviewSummary: Limits SPLRC activities to approved plans, restricts deceptive corporate names, and sets incorporator residency and stock par value minimums.

headings.title: Operational activities restricted to plan of operation
headings.reviewNote: Restricts SPLRC activities strictly to those necessary to accomplish purposes outlined in its approved plan of operation.

headings.title: Name restrictions and deceptiveness prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits SPLRC names that are deceptively similar to or likely to be confused with existing registered Missouri business names.

headings.title: Minimum incorporator and state residency requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires at least three incorporators or organizers, with at least one being a resident of Missouri.

headings.title: Capital stock issuance at not less than par
headings.reviewNote: Requires capital stock of an SPLRC incorporated as a stock company to be issued at not less than par value.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs SPLRC securities and surplus notes issuance, statutory surplus accounting, debt repayment formulas, and risk alignment standards.

headings.title: Authority to issue securities and perform contracts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes an SPLRC to issue securities and enter necessary contracts in accordance with its plan of operation and applicable law.

headings.title: Accounting for surplus notes and repayment approvals
headings.reviewNote: Allows surplus notes to be accounted for as statutory surplus with prior director approval for interest and principal payments.

headings.title: Approval of formulas for debt service payments
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to approve formulas for ongoing payment of interest and principal on SPLRC securities.

headings.title: Risk alignment for debt service obligations
headings.reviewNote: Requires repayment obligations on SPLRC securities to reflect the underwriting risks assumed under reinsurance contracts.

headings.title: Modification or revocation of debt service approval
headings.reviewNote: Limits revocation or modification of debt service approvals to instances where adverse experience threatens contract fulfillment.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines recognized admitted assets on SPLRC statements and establishes statutory valuation methods for letters of credit and guarantee instruments.

headings.title: Recognized admitted assets on financial statements
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates admitted assets for SPLRC financial statements including permitted investments, letters of credit, AAA guarantee policies, and surety bonds.

headings.title: Valuation methods for letters of credit and securities
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes valuation rules for letters of credit, guarantees, and surety bonds, authorizing alternative methods by director order.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs dividend declarations by SPLRCs, prohibiting capital impairment and conditioning payouts on approved surplus formulas and obligation fulfillment.

headings.title: Dividend declarations restricted to transaction agreements
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits SPLRC dividend declarations or distributions except in accordance with approved transaction agreements.

headings.title: Capital impairment prohibition for dividend payments
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits dividend payments that would reduce SPLRC capital below required minimum initial capital thresholds.

headings.title: Sufficiency of remaining assets to satisfy obligations
headings.reviewNote: Requires remaining SPLRC assets and trust funds to be sufficient to satisfy the director that obligations will be met after dividends.

headings.title: Conditions for ongoing dividend distribution approvals
headings.reviewNote: Conditions director approval of ongoing dividends on maintaining capital and surplus equal to approved formulas.

headings.title: Management dividend declarations and statutory compliance
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes management to declare dividends provided the payments comply with statutory limits and do not jeopardize obligations.

entries.reviewSummary: Enacts Missouri's valued policy law for real property total losses, specifying coverage exceptions, pro rata multi-policy allocations, and commercial building limits.

headings.title: Valued policy measure of recovery for total loss
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that insurer liability for total loss of real property by covered peril equals the policy limit less any deductible.

headings.title: Statutory exemptions from valued policy provisions
headings.reviewNote: Exempts partial losses, unscheduled personalty, appurtenant structures, builder's risks, mortgage insurance, and criminal acts of insureds.

headings.title: Proportional contribution among multiple property policies
headings.reviewNote: Provides that when two or more policies cover a total loss of real property, insureds may recover the face amount of the policy with the highest coverage limit, with each policy contributing proportionally.

headings.title: Valuation rules for policies covering multiple buildings
headings.reviewNote: Directs that total loss to a commercial building insured on a blanket basis covering two or more commercial buildings be settled based on the initial pre-loss value assigned to each affected building, with any balance settled per policy terms.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates annual independent CPA-audited financial reports within five months of fiscal year end and March first statutory accounting financial filings for SPLRCs.

headings.title: Annual CPA-audited financial report filing
headings.reviewNote: Requires a SPLRC to file an independent CPA-audited financial report of its financial statements and reserve-credit trust accounts within five months after its fiscal year end.

headings.title: Annual March first statutory accounting financial filing
headings.reviewNote: Requires a SPLRC to file statutory accounting financial information by March first each year, including income statement, balance sheet, and if required an invested-assets listing, plus optional RBC/adjusted capital calculations and required contract performance assessments.

entries.reviewSummary: Imposes tiered reinsurance premium taxes on SPLRCs, establishing minimum and maximum limits, fee deductions, local preemption, and revenue allocations.

headings.title: Tiered premium tax rates on assumed reinsurance
headings.reviewNote: Imposes tiered annual premium taxes on SPLRC assumed reinsurance premiums ranging from 0.214 percent to 0.024 percent with common-control transfer exceptions.

headings.title: Preemption of local taxes and ad valorem exception
headings.reviewNote: Declares state premium taxes in lieu of all other state and local taxes, except ad valorem property taxes.

headings.title: Minimum and maximum annual aggregate tax limits
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a minimum annual premium tax of $7,500 and a maximum annual aggregate tax of $200,000 for SPLRCs.

headings.title: Deduction and carryforward of licensing fees
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes deducting application, licensing, and renewal fees from premium taxes, allowing up to five years of nonrefundable carryforward.

headings.title: Annual tax return filing and assessment procedure
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual premium tax returns by February first, director certification by March thirty-first, and revenue assessment.

headings.title: Delinquency penalties for late returns and tax payments
headings.reviewNote: Subjects SPLRCs failing to file timely returns or pay taxes to statutory interest and delinquency penalties under chapter 148.

headings.title: Allocation of collected taxes to general revenue
headings.reviewNote: Allocates ninety percent of collected SPLRC taxes to general revenue and ten percent to the insurance dedicated fund, subject to caps.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes specialized insolvency procedures for SPLRCs, protecting assets and contract recoveries from ceding insurer insolvency proceedings.

headings.title: Judicial grounds for conservation rehabilitation or liquidation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to petition circuit court to conserve, rehabilitate, or liquidate an SPLRC for asset dissipation or consensual insolvency.

headings.title: Clear and convincing evidence burden for asset dissipation
headings.reviewNote: Imposes a clear and convincing evidence standard of proof on the director for petitions alleging asset dissipation or diversion.

headings.title: Receiver asset management under special captive statutes
headings.reviewNote: Directs receivers to manage SPLRC assets and liabilities under sections 379.1353 to 379.1421 notwithstanding other insolvency laws.

headings.title: Non-reduction of reinsurance recoveries upon ceding insolvency
headings.reviewNote: Provides that amounts recoverable by a receiver under an SPLRC contract shall not be reduced by ceding company insolvency.

headings.title: Non-interruption of business by ceding company proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Protects SPLRC operations and payments from injunctions or stays arising from ceding insurer insolvency proceedings in any state.

headings.title: Protection of debt service payments in summary proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Shields SPLRC payments on securities and contracts from prohibition by court orders in interim summary proceedings.

headings.title: Bar against voiding nonfraudulent contract transfers
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits receivers of ceding insurers or SPLRCs from voiding nonfraudulent contract transfers or security payments.

headings.title: Prohibition of asset consolidation with ceding company
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits consolidating SPLRC assets, trusts, or guarantees into a ceding insurer's estate in delinquency proceedings.

headings.title: Conduct of delinquency proceedings under chapter 375
headings.reviewNote: Directs that SPLRC delinquency proceedings not specifically governed by this section be conducted under general insurance insolvency laws.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires specialty vendor licensing to sell portable electronics insurance, establishing application procedures, responsible person designations, and fees.

headings.title: Vendor license requirement for portable electronics insurance
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits vendors from selling or soliciting portable electronics insurance coverage without obtaining a specialty license.

headings.title: Application contents and designated responsible person
headings.reviewNote: Requires license application identifying a designated responsible employee or officer and authorizes sales at all vendor retail locations.

headings.title: Initial and renewal licensing fees for vendors
headings.reviewNote: Establishes initial license fees up to $1,000 and renewal fees up to $500, with receipts deposited in the insurance dedicated fund.

headings.title: License expiration and automatic termination
headings.reviewNote: Provides that unrenewed portable electronics insurance licenses terminate automatically on their expiration date without producer grace periods.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates portable electronics insurance marketing, detailing point-of-sale brochures, underwriting records, supervising business entities, complaint sharing, location registries, training, and fiduciary premium handling.

headings.title: Mandatory consumer disclosure brochures at retail locations
headings.reviewNote: Requires point-of-sale brochures disclosing potential duplicate coverage, optional enrollment, coverage terms, claims processes, and cancellation rights.

headings.title: Program underwriting standards and primary coverage status
headings.reviewNote: Requires five-year maintenance of underwriting records and designates portable electronics insurance as primary coverage with mandatory disclosures.

headings.title: Supervising business entity appointment and duties
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurers to appoint a licensed supervising business entity to oversee vendor compliance, training, and customer communications.

headings.title: Sharing of vendor compliance complaints and inquiries
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurers and supervising business entities to share all complaints, grievances, or inquiries regarding vendor-specific conduct that may not comply with state laws and regulations.

headings.title: Maintenance and inspection of vendor location registry
headings.reviewNote: Requires supervising business entities to maintain a registry of authorized Missouri vendor locations open to director inspection upon ten days' notice during regular business hours.

headings.title: Registry termination updates and disciplinary reporting
headings.reviewNote: Requires updating the registry within thirty days of terminating a vendor location's appointment and reporting section 375.141 disciplinary causes to the director in writing with section 375.022 immunities.

headings.title: Prohibition on registry addition or removal fees
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits a supervising business entity from charging a fee for adding or removing a vendor location from the registry.

headings.title: Prohibition on unlicensed representation as insurance producer
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits vendor employees or authorized representatives from advertising or holding themselves out as insurance producers unless otherwise licensed as insurance producers.

headings.title: Delivery of electronic and supplemental training programs
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes electronic delivery of required employee training supplemented by licensed educational oversight.

headings.title: Collection and fiduciary handling of insurance charges
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes vendors to bill and collect insurance charges, itemizing premiums and holding collected funds in trust for insurers.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes the director to suspend, revoke, or restrict portable electronics vendor licenses and sanction individual locations or representatives.

headings.title: Grounds for suspension revocation or refusal to issue
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to suspend, revoke, or refuse to issue or renew vendor licenses for any section 375.141 reason or for deceptive advertising, fraudulent fee collection, or breach of professional trust; source note records repeated phrase 'refuse to issue, or refuse to issue' in original rolls.

headings.title: Location-specific suspensions and representative sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the director to suspend insurance transactions at specific retail locations or revoke privileges of individual employee representatives.

entries.reviewSummary: Grants administrative rulemaking authority for portable electronics insurance under chapter 536 and sets the January 1, 2012 effective date.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and chapter 536 compliance
headings.reviewNote: Grants rulemaking authority to the director under chapter 536 procedures and establishes nonseverability provisions.

headings.title: Effective date of portable electronics insurance act
headings.reviewNote: Establishes an effective date of January 1, 2012, for the portable electronics insurance regulatory act.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates standard fire policy filings, sixty-day loss notice requirements, adjuster waiver rules, coinsurance credits, and property valuation estoppels.

headings.title: Standard fire insurance policy filing and approval
headings.reviewNote: Requires fire insurance companies to file policy forms with the director for approval and designate Missouri standard fire policies.

headings.title: Printed company address and notice of loss
headings.reviewNote: Requires printing a United States office address on fire policies to which loss notices must be sent within sixty days.

headings.title: Waiver of notice coinsurance and real property value
headings.reviewNote: Deems adjuster appearance a waiver of loss notice, authorizes coinsurance credits, and prohibits denying property value at policy issuance.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates limited lines self-service storage insurance, detailing producer licensing, point-of-sale disclosures, policy limits, and rulemaking.

headings.title: Definitions for self-service storage insurance
headings.reviewNote: Defines department, director, limited lines self-service storage insurance producer, offer and disseminate, and self-service storage insurance.

headings.title: Producer licensing requirements and retail disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Sets licensing standards, employee registry requirements, brochure disclosures, fee itemization, and prohibited conduct for unlicensed staff.

headings.title: Authorization of registered representatives and compensation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes registered employees and representatives of limited lines storage producers to disseminate policies and receive compensation.

headings.title: Issuance under individual or master group policies
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes self-service storage insurance coverage to be issued under individual policies or master group policies.

headings.title: Application of insurance department regulatory chapters
headings.reviewNote: Subjects limited lines storage producers and representatives to regulatory enforcement under chapters 374 and 375 except as modified.

headings.title: Maximum coverage limitation per storage unit
headings.reviewNote: Caps self-service storage insurance coverage at fifteen thousand dollars per customer per individual storage unit.

headings.title: Promulgation of administrative rules and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Grants rulemaking authority to the director under chapter 536 and establishes nonseverability provisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates tiered primary automobile coverage for transportation network company drivers, specifying digital network and ride limits, lapse duties, and proof.

headings.title: Mandatory primary insurance for network company drivers
headings.reviewNote: Requires transportation network company (TNC) drivers or companies to maintain primary coverage for digital network and ride stages.

headings.title: Coverage requirements while logged on to network
headings.reviewNote: Sets minimum liability limits of $50,000/$100,000/$25,000 and uninsured motorist coverage while logged on without a ride request.

headings.title: Coverage requirements during prearranged rides
headings.reviewNote: Requires primary automobile liability insurance of at least one million dollars and uninsured motorist coverage during prearranged rides.

headings.title: First dollar company coverage upon driver lapse
headings.reviewNote: Requires TNC policy to provide first-dollar coverage and defense if driver insurance lapses, or excess coverage if driver limits fall short.

headings.title: Personal insurer denial not required for coverage
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that coverage under a TNC policy is not contingent upon prior denial of a claim by the driver's personal automobile insurer.

headings.title: Authorized and surplus lines insurer placements
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes TNC insurance placement with licensed Missouri automobile insurers or eligible surplus lines insurers under chapter 384.

headings.title: Satisfaction of motor vehicle financial responsibility laws
headings.reviewNote: Deems insurance meeting statutory TNC requirements compliant with motor vehicle financial responsibility mandates under chapter 303.

headings.title: Duty to carry and produce proof of coverage
headings.reviewNote: Requires drivers to carry proof of coverage and disclose digital network status to interested parties, insurers, and investigating officers.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes personal automobile insurers to exclude commercial transportation network activities, establishes contribution rights, and mandates data sharing.

headings.title: Permissible personal automobile policy exclusions for TNC
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes personal automobile insurers to exclude coverage while a vehicle is logged on to a TNC digital network or providing rides.

headings.title: Scope of permissible automobile coverage exclusions
headings.reviewNote: Outlines permissible exclusions across liability, uninsured motorist, medical payments, comprehensive, and collision coverages.

headings.title: Optional endorsement coverage for commercial ridesharing
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that personal insurers may elect to provide rideshare coverage by express policy contract or endorsement.

headings.title: Duty to defend and preserve prior commercial exclusions
headings.reviewNote: Relieves insurers of defense and indemnity duties for excluded TNC claims and preserves traditional livery and commercial exclusions.

headings.title: Insurer right of contribution for excluded claims
headings.reviewNote: Grants automobile insurers that defend or indemnify excluded claims a right of contribution against statutory TNC insurers.

headings.title: Information exchange cooperation during claims investigations
headings.reviewNote: Requires TNC companies and insurers to cooperate and share log-on records and policy limits during accident coverage investigations.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines authorized employer, union, and association groups for personal lines property and casualty insurance and sets standards for discretionary groups.

headings.title: Eligible groups for personal lines property casualty
headings.reviewNote: Defines eligible groups for group personal lines property and casualty insurance, including employer, labor union, and qualifying association groups.

headings.title: Discretionary group approval and public interest findings
headings.reviewNote: Permits personal lines group policies for non-enumerated groups upon director findings of public interest, administrative economy, and reasonable rates.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates group personal lines master policies and certificates, requiring prior form approval, mandatory policy terms, and employee premium protections.

headings.title: Issuance of master policy and coverage certificates
headings.reviewNote: Requires issuance of a master policy to the group policyholder and individual certificates of coverage to insured employees or members.

headings.title: Prior filing and approval of policy forms
headings.reviewNote: Requires master policy forms, endorsements, riders, and certificate forms to satisfy statutory filing requirements prior to delivery.

headings.title: Mandatory provisions of personal lines master policy
headings.reviewNote: Specifies required terms in the master policy regarding premium collection, eligibility periods, effective dates, termination, and conversions.

headings.title: Protection of insureds upon policyholder remittance failure
headings.reviewNote: Protects individual employees or members from cancellation for nonpayment when their contributions have been timely deducted by the policyholder.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates basic coverage packages, initial thirty-one day enrollment periods, class-wide reduction rules, termination grounds, and anti-stacking provisions.

headings.title: Basic coverage package and optional supplemental limits
headings.reviewNote: Mandates a basic package of statutory minimum coverages for all eligible group members and authorizes optional supplemental coverages.

headings.title: Initial eligibility enrollment period and underwriting
headings.reviewNote: Guarantees coverage for eligible members electing coverage within an initial thirty-one day period, subjecting late applicants to underwriting.

headings.title: Class-wide coverage reductions limited to statutory minimums
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits individual coverage reductions, permitting reductions only class-wide and never below statutory minimum requirements.

headings.title: Exclusive statutory grounds for terminating group coverage
headings.reviewNote: Restricts individual coverage termination to nonpayment, group master termination, class discontinuance, or termination of employment.

headings.title: Policyholder election of optional coverages and limits
headings.reviewNote: Makes policyholder selection or rejection of statutory optional coverages binding on group members upon written disclosure.

headings.title: Prohibition of stacking coverages across policies
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits stacking coverages or limits among separate certificates of insurance under a group personal lines master policy, except applying state individual-policy stacking law to separate certificates issued to relatives living in the same household.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires rating plan filings for group personal lines master policies, defines non-discriminatory group rating adjustments, and regulates experience refunds and dividends.

headings.title: Filing requirement for master policy rating plans
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits issuing or delivering a master policy or certificate unless the rating plan and amendments used to determine master policy premium have met applicable state filing requirements.

headings.title: Permissible group rating factors and non-discrimination
headings.reviewNote: Provides that group premium rates are not unfairly discriminatory if adjusted for loss experience or group expense factors, averaged broadly, or omitting individual policy surcharges and discounts.

headings.title: Experience refunds and dividends for insureds' benefit
headings.reviewNote: Permits paying experience refunds or dividends to the group policyholder when justified by experience, requiring any excess over the policyholder's premium contribution to be applied solely for insured employees or members.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates separate loss and expense statistics for group personal lines, bars compulsory participation and tied sales, includes group data in residual market calculations, and sets premium tax allocation rules.

headings.title: Separate loss and expense experience statistics
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurers issuing or delivering group personal lines property and casualty insurance to maintain separate loss and expense experience statistics.

headings.title: Prohibition on compulsory purchase or nonparticipation penalties
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits issuing or delivering a group personal lines policy if purchase is a condition of employment or group membership or if nonparticipation subjects an employee or member to penalty.

headings.title: Prohibition on tied sales with safety and package exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits conditioning group policy purchase on buying another product or service or vice versa, while permitting reasonable safety-device requirements and package or combination policies.

headings.title: Inclusion of group experience in residual market plans
headings.reviewNote: Directs that an insurer's group personal lines property and casualty experience be included when determining participation in applicable residual market plans.

headings.title: Premium tax allocation and interstate apportionment
headings.reviewNote: Requires allocating group premiums for premium tax purposes under individual personal lines rules, allowing annual insured surveys and apportioning among states without differentiating policyholder or member contributions.

entries.reviewSummary: Exempts group policyholders from insurance agent licensing for administrative functions and eliminates countersignature mandates.

headings.title: Producer licensing requirement and administrative exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Requires producer licensure under sections 375.012 to 375.146 to solicit, negotiate, or sell group personal lines policies, while exempting specified endorsement, information distribution, payroll deduction, and expense-reimbursement activities without superseding anti-rebating or commission-splitting laws.

headings.title: Countersignature law exemptions for group certificates
headings.reviewNote: Exempts group personal lines policies and individual certificates from statutory Missouri countersignature requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Guarantees individual conversion rights upon termination of employment or group membership, setting notice and application deadlines.

headings.title: Thirty-day written notice of termination and conversion options
headings.reviewNote: Requires thirty days' prior written notice stating discontinuance reasons and individual conversion options when a covered employee's or member's coverage terminates other than for nonpayment or by request.

headings.title: Conversion right to individual policy within thirty days
headings.reviewNote: Entitles a terminated or ineligible employee or member who applies and pays the first premium within thirty days of notice to an individual policy from the insurer or an affiliate with at least statutory minimum coverages and limits.

headings.title: Exemption when master policy replaced within thirty days
headings.reviewNote: Eliminates individual termination notice and conversion privileges if the master policy is replaced by another master policy within thirty days, with prior coverage terminating when the replacement takes effect.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires insurer licensure or eligible nonadmitted status for group personal lines policies, excludes mass marketing, credit, personal auto, and chapter 384 nonadmitted policies, preserves director authority over out-of-state policies, and grants rulemaking authority.

headings.title: Insurer licensing or eligible nonadmitted status requirement
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits issuing or delivering a master policy or certificate in Missouri unless the insurer is duly licensed for the covered lines or is an eligible nonadmitted insurer under section 384.021.

headings.title: Inapplicability to mass marketing of individual policies
headings.reviewNote: Excludes mass marketing or any other marketing of individual personal lines property and casualty insurance policies from sections 379.1800 to 379.1824.

headings.title: Inapplicability to credit property and credit casualty policies
headings.reviewNote: Excludes credit property and credit casualty policies insuring a creditor's debtors with respect to their indebtedness from sections 379.1800 to 379.1824.

headings.title: Inapplicability to personal automobile and motor vehicle policies
headings.reviewNote: Excludes personal automobile and personal motor vehicle liability policies from sections 379.1800 to 379.1824 and clarifies those sections do not authorize group personal auto policies.

headings.title: Exemption for policies issued by chapter 384 nonadmitted insurers
headings.reviewNote: Exempts policies issued by a nonadmitted insurer pursuant to chapter 384 from sections 379.1800 to 379.1812.

headings.title: Preservation of director authority over out-of-state master policies
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that sections 379.1800 to 379.1824 do not limit the director's authority regarding Missouri resident complaints or disputes under master policies issued or delivered in another state.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority under chapter 536 and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to promulgate rules to implement sections 379.1800 to 379.1824 subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028, with a post-August 28, 2021 nonseverability clause.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs applicability of lender-placed insurance statutes to mortgaged real property and defines commercial and optional loan exemptions.

headings.title: Application to lender-placed insurance transactions
headings.reviewNote: Applies sections 379.1850 to 379.1869 to insurers and insurance producers engaging in lender-placed insurance transactions.

headings.title: Exemptions from lender-placed insurance regulations
headings.reviewNote: Exempts commercial loans, mortgagor-elected optional insurance, lender-owned real estate policies, and uncharged insurance.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs effective dates, automatic termination events, and billing limitations for mortgaged real property lender-placed insurance.

headings.title: Permissible effective date of lender-placed insurance
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits lender-placed insurance from becoming effective earlier than the actual date coverage lapsed under the mortgage agreement.

headings.title: Termination dates for individual lender-placed insurance
headings.reviewNote: Directs termination of lender-placed policies upon receipt of acceptable replacement insurance, mortgage payoff, or policy expiration.

headings.title: Limitations on premium charges and retroactive billing
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits charging mortgagors for terms longer than scheduled coverage or billing premiums prior to the policy effective date.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes replacement cost valuation hierarchies, requires payment of excess claim proceeds to mortgagors, and enforces filed rates.

headings.title: Replacement cost basis and hierarchy of determination
headings.reviewNote: Requires coverage to be based on replacement cost value, following a hierarchy of last known amount, insurer calculation, or loan balance.

headings.title: Payment of excess loss proceeds to mortgagor
headings.reviewNote: Requires loss proceeds exceeding the unpaid mortgage loan balance to be paid directly to the mortgagor.

headings.title: Mandatory adherence to filed rate schedules
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits insurers from writing lender-placed insurance at rates differing from rate schedules filed with the insurance department.
