entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits conflicts of interest, servicer commissions, premium sharing, contingent profits, and improper outsourcing in lender-placed insurance.

headings.title: Prohibited issuance on servicer-affiliated mortgaged properties
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits insurers or producers from issuing lender-placed insurance on mortgaged property serviced or owned by them or their affiliates.

headings.title: Prohibition of commissions and compensation to lenders
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits compensating lenders, servicers, or investors through commissions or payments for lender-placed insurance policies.

headings.title: Prohibition of premium or risk sharing arrangements
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits insurers or producers from sharing lender-placed insurance premiums or underwriting risks with lenders or servicers.

headings.title: Prohibition of contingent commissions and profit sharing
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits offering contingent commissions, profit-sharing, or loss-ratio payments to any person affiliated with a servicer or insurer.

headings.title: Restrictions on free or discounted outsourced services
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits insurers from providing below-cost services to lenders or outsourcing insurer functions to lenders at inflated rates.

headings.title: Prohibition of payments to secure insurance business
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits making payments or expense reimbursements to lenders or servicers for the purpose of securing lender-placed insurance business.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs lender-placed policy and rate filings, department rate review, quadrennial refilings, separate REO rates, annual reporting, low-loss-ratio refilings, and general filing compliance.

headings.title: Mandatory filing of policy forms and rate schedules
headings.reviewNote: Requires all lender-placed policy forms, certificates, and premium rate schedules to be filed with the department of commerce and insurance.

headings.title: Department rate review for excessiveness and adequacy
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to review lender-placed rates and expense allowances to ensure rates are not excessive, inadequate, or discriminatory.

headings.title: Mandatory rate refiling every four years
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurers writing lender-placed insurance to refile their premium rates with the department at least once every four years.

headings.title: Separate rates for voluntary and lender-placed policies
headings.reviewNote: Requires distinct rate filings for lender-placed insurance and voluntary coverage purchased on real estate owned property.

headings.title: Actuarial standards and experience data in rate filings
headings.reviewNote: Governs actuarial support for new programs, authorizing reliance on company experience, catastrophe models, and federal flood data.

headings.title: Annual calendar year financial reporting requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurers with $100,000 or more in direct written premium to file detailed annual loss ratio and expense reports by April first.

headings.title: Mandatory rate filing after consecutive low loss ratios
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurers experiencing an annual loss ratio below thirty-five percent in a lender-placed program for two consecutive years to submit an adjusting or supporting rate filing within ninety days of annual reporting, excluding flood insurance.

headings.title: Compliance with general state rate and form filing laws
headings.reviewNote: Directs that except as specifically set forth in this section, lender-placed rates and forms be filed as required under Missouri insurance laws.

entries.reviewSummary: Grants the director chapter 374 enforcement authority with Cole County judicial review, disclaims private causes of action, and preserves existing mortgagor legal rights.

headings.title: Director enforcement powers and administrative sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to enforce sections 379.1850 to 379.1869 under chapter 374, subjects final orders to chapter 536 judicial review in Cole County circuit court, and preserves liability under other state laws.

headings.title: No private cause of action created or implied
headings.reviewNote: Provides that nothing in sections 379.1850 to 379.1869 creates or implies a private cause of action for statutory violations.

headings.title: Preservation of existing mortgagor legal rights
headings.reviewNote: Provides that nothing in sections 379.1850 to 379.1869 extinguishes any mortgagor rights otherwise available under state, federal, or common law.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes primary liability insurance requirements for peer-to-peer car sharing, detailing program coverage, lapse duties, and dispute assumptions.

headings.title: Program assumption of shared vehicle owner liability
headings.reviewNote: Requires a peer-to-peer car-sharing program, subject to subsection 2, to assume a shared vehicle owner's liability for third-party bodily injury/property damage, uninsured/underinsured motorist losses, and required PIP losses at no less than chapter 303 limits.

headings.title: Exceptions to program assumption of owner liability
headings.reviewNote: Exempts a car-sharing program from assuming liability for a shared vehicle owner who makes an intentional or fraudulent material misrepresentation/omission or acts in concert with a driver failing to return the vehicle.

headings.title: Third-party loss coverage under assumed liability
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that, notwithstanding the definition of car-sharing termination time, subsection 1 liability assumption applies to specified losses by damaged third parties as required by chapter 303.

headings.title: Minimum chapter 303 liability coverage during sharing
headings.reviewNote: Requires the car-sharing program to ensure the owner and driver are insured during each car-sharing period at no less than chapter 303 minimum limits under a policy recognizing car sharing or not excluding shared vehicle drivers.

headings.title: Satisfaction of insurance obligations by program participants
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes coverage requirements to be satisfied by insurance maintained by the shared vehicle owner, driver, program, or combination.

headings.title: Primary insurance status during car-sharing period
headings.reviewNote: Designates the insurance maintaining coverage as primary during each car-sharing period, covering out-of-state statutory limit differences.

headings.title: Program assumption of primary liability during disputes
headings.reviewNote: Mandates program assumption of primary liability when control disputes exist or when records regarding vehicle return locations are missing.

headings.title: First-dollar program coverage upon participant lapse
headings.reviewNote: Requires program insurance to provide first-dollar coverage and defense if owner or driver insurance lapses or fails to provide required limits.

headings.title: Program coverage independent of personal insurer denial
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that program insurance coverage is not dependent upon prior denial of a claim by a personal automobile insurer.

headings.title: Retention of program liability for acts and indemnification
headings.reviewNote: Preserves program liability for its own acts and permits contractual indemnification actions against owners or drivers for agreement breaches.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes personal automobile insurers to exclude peer-to-peer car-sharing activities and preserves general underwriting and cancellation rights.

headings.title: Permissible personal motor vehicle policy exclusions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes personal motor vehicle insurers to exclude coverage and duty to defend for claims arising during peer-to-peer car-sharing periods.

headings.title: Preservation of existing commercial and rental exclusions
headings.reviewNote: Preserves existing policy exclusions for vehicles rented, shared, hired, or used for commercial purposes.

headings.title: Insurer underwriting and cancellation authority preserved
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that car-sharing statutes do not restrict an insurer's right to underwrite, cancel, or nonrenew personal motor vehicle policies.

entries.reviewSummary: Recognizes an insurable interest for car-sharing programs during car-sharing periods and authorizes program group liability policies.

headings.title: Statutory insurable interest in shared vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that peer-to-peer car-sharing programs possess an insurable interest in shared vehicles during car-sharing periods.

headings.title: Program coverage obligations limited to statute
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that establishing an insurable interest does not create liability on programs beyond statutory insurance mandates.

headings.title: Authority to maintain group or master liability policies
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes car-sharing programs to maintain insurance policies covering program liabilities, owner liabilities, vehicle damages, and driver liabilities.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes absolute liability of casualty insurers upon occurrence of a covered loss and invalidates post-loss cancellation agreements.

headings.title: Absolute liability of insurer upon casualty loss
headings.reviewNote: Makes insurer liability absolute upon occurrence of a covered accident or death, independent of final judgment satisfaction or insured bankruptcy.

headings.title: Post-loss agreement cancelling or annulling policy void
headings.reviewNote: Declares void any agreement between insurer and insured to cancel or annul an insurance policy after liability for a loss has attached.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires driver's license verification before entering peer-to-peer car-sharing agreements and mandates driver data retention.

headings.title: Driver license verification requirements for car sharing
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits car-sharing programs from entering agreements unless operating drivers hold valid domestic or foreign driver's licenses.

headings.title: Recordkeeping and driver data retention requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires programs to record driver names, addresses, license numbers, and place of issuance, retaining records as required by law.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires peer-to-peer car-sharing programs to verify open safety recalls and notify owners, and bars shared vehicle owners from making recalled vehicles available before repair.

headings.title: Program verification of open safety recalls and notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires a peer-to-peer car-sharing program, at registration and before a vehicle is made available, to verify there are no unrepaired safety recalls and notify the owner of subsection 2 duties.

headings.title: Shared vehicle owner duties upon safety recall notice
headings.reviewNote: Bars an owner with actual recall notice from making the vehicle available until repaired, requires removing an available vehicle as soon as practicable until repaired, and requires notifying the program if recalled while in a driver's possession.

entries.reviewSummary: Enacts mandatory uninsured motorist coverage requirements including hit-and-run and insolvent-insurer protection, establishes subrogation rights, and sets prima facie evidentiary rules for uninsured status.

headings.title: Mandatory uninsured motorist coverage and limits
headings.reviewNote: Requires automobile liability policies (or offers for commercial vehicles and five-plus passenger fleets) to include uninsured motorist bodily injury/death coverage at chapter 303 limits, including unidentified hit-and-run vehicles regardless of physical contact.

headings.title: Insolvent liability insurer included as uninsured vehicle
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'uninsured motor vehicle' to include, subject to policy terms, an insured motor vehicle whose liability insurer is unable to pay its insured's legal liability within specified limits due to insolvency.

headings.title: Two-year insolvency window and more favorable terms
headings.reviewNote: Limits insolvency protection to accidents during the policy period where the tort-feasor's liability insurer becomes insolvent within two years after the accident, while allowing insurers to offer more favorable terms.

headings.title: Insurer subrogation and recovery against tortfeasors
headings.reviewNote: Grants insurers paying uninsured motorist claims subrogation to settlement or judgment proceeds, including insolvent insurer assets, while limiting insolvency-coverage recovery against the tort-feasor to proceeds from the insolvent insurer's assets.

headings.title: Prima facie evidence of uninsured status from reports
headings.reviewNote: Makes failure to file a section 303.040 report (established by certified director of revenue statement) or a filed report showing no coverage prima facie evidence of uninsured status in policy actions.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs submission of mutual articles to the director, publication and attorney general approval, secretary of state certification, and article amendments.

headings.title: Submission of mutual articles to director
headings.reviewNote: Requires articles of association for a mutual insurance company to be submitted to the director of the department of commerce and insurance.

headings.title: Publication attorney general approval and recording
headings.reviewNote: Requires publication under section 379.030 and attorney general approval under section 379.040, after which the director records the articles and provides certified copies to the incorporators and secretary of state.

headings.title: Issuance of certificate of incorporation by secretary
headings.reviewNote: Directs the secretary of state to issue a certificate of incorporation to the company as its authority to begin business.

headings.title: Amendment of mutual articles of association
headings.reviewNote: Permits amending the articles of association in the manner provided for other corporations or as provided in the articles.

entries.reviewSummary: Begins mutual corporate existence upon certification, authorizes bylaws and applications while barring insurance in force prior to licensing, and mandates thirty-day bylaw filings.

headings.title: Corporate existence upon issuance of certificate
headings.reviewNote: Vests corporate powers and begins corporate existence upon issuance of the certificate of incorporation by the secretary of state.

headings.title: Board adoption of bylaws and pre-license insurance bar
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the named board of directors to adopt bylaws, accept applications, and transact business while barring putting insurance in force until licensed under sections 379.205 to 379.310; source note indicates section 379.310 was repealed in 1967.

headings.title: Filing of bylaws and amendments with director
headings.reviewNote: Requires bylaws and any amendments to be filed with the director within thirty days after adoption.

entries.reviewSummary: Prescribes minimum membership, single-risk limits, paid premiums, and surplus assets for mutual insurers, with phase-in relief and revocation sanctions.

headings.title: Mandatory prerequisites for mutual policy issuance
headings.reviewNote: Requires mutual insurers to hold at least twenty bona fide applications covering two hundred separate risks, capital, and surplus funds.

headings.title: Temporary license renewal exception for existing mutuals
headings.reviewNote: Permits non-life, non-fire mutuals licensed as of September 28, 1977, to renew licenses through 1979 maintaining $300,000 in assets.

headings.title: Certificate revocation for violation of mutual prerequisites
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to revoke the certificate of authority of any mutual insurer violating section prerequisites.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes public and private entities to hold mutual insurance policies, protects corporate officers from personal liability, and confirms corporate powers.

headings.title: Public and private entity authority to hold policies
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes public or private corporations, boards, and associations to apply for and hold policies in mutual insurance companies.

headings.title: Representative capacity of officers and liability immunity
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes corporate officers and trustees to act for entity members without incurring personal liability on mutual policies.

headings.title: Corporate membership power declared incidental to purpose
headings.reviewNote: Declares the right of Missouri corporations to hold mutual insurance policies to be incidental to corporate purposes and fully granted.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates mutual premium structures, requiring maximum premium disclosures and setting minimum surplus thresholds for non-assessable policies.

headings.title: Expression of maximum premium in policy or application
headings.reviewNote: Requires the maximum premium payable by any mutual member to be clearly expressed in the policy or insurance application.

headings.title: Permissible cash and contingent premium structures
headings.reviewNote: Permits maximum premiums to consist of cash premiums with contingent liability or strictly cash premiums without assessments.

headings.title: Surplus requirement for non-assessable cash-only policies
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits issuing non-assessable policies without contingent premiums unless the mutual holds surplus equal to capital required for stock companies.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes directors, officers, and members to advance operating funds to mutual insurers payable only from surplus, barring commissions.

headings.title: Advances of money to mutual companies
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes directors, officers, or members to advance funds to mutual companies at interest not exceeding ten percent payable solely from surplus.

headings.title: Prohibition of commissions on financial advances
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits paying commissions or promotion expenses on financial advances and requires reporting advances in annual statements.

entries.reviewSummary: Exempts commission-free mutual policies from resident agent countersignature laws and permits consistent plan-specific policy provisions.

headings.title: Exemption from resident agent countersignature laws
headings.reviewNote: Exempts mutual insurance policies from resident agent countersignature laws if no commission is paid to a local agent.

headings.title: Inclusion of plan-specific policy provisions
headings.reviewNote: Permits mutual insurers to insert plan-specific provisions in prescribed policy forms so long as they do not conflict with state law.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates annual premium tax returns for mutuals, setting verification schedules, suspension penalties for nonpayment, and fund allocations.

headings.title: Annual gross direct premium tax returns
headings.reviewNote: Requires mutual insurers to file annual sworn premium tax returns by March first detailing gross direct premiums and statutory credits.

headings.title: Director verification and assessment schedule
headings.reviewNote: Directs the insurance director to verify returns, assess premium taxes, and file certified schedules with revenue by April first.

headings.title: Notice and deadline for tax payment
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director of revenue to notify insurers of assessed taxes payable on or before May first.

headings.title: Suspension of delinquent companies from business
headings.reviewNote: Directs the insurance director to suspend delinquent insurers from transacting business in Missouri until unpaid premium taxes are satisfied.

headings.title: Deposit and allocation of collected taxes
headings.reviewNote: Directs deposit of collected premium taxes, allocating half to state general revenue and half to the county foreign insurance tax fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Delineates fire and marine rating law scope and exclusions, defines inland marine insurance, and cross-references commercial property and casualty filing rules under section 379.321.

headings.title: Scope and application of rating law
headings.reviewNote: Applies section 379.017 and sections 379.316 to 379.361 to fire, allied lines, marine, inland marine, and combination policies, excluding reinsurance (except joint reinsurance), ocean marine, aircraft, motor vehicle, and life/health/workers' compensation; source notes record repealed sections 379.355 and 379.310.

headings.title: Definition and scope of inland marine insurance
headings.reviewNote: Provides that inland marine insurance includes insurance defined as such by statute, interpretation, director ruling, or general business custom.

headings.title: Commercial property and casualty filing requirements
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that commercial property and commercial casualty insurance policies are subject to rate and form filing requirements as provided in section 379.321.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates rate and form filings within ten days of use, excess-rate consent, rating organization authorization and withdrawal, six-month change reviews, and commercial property and casualty filing exemptions and notices.

headings.title: Premium rate and policy form filing
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing manuals, rules, rates, rating plans, modifications, and forms (except commercial lines under subsection 6) directly or via a licensed rating organization, with filing within ten days after effective date constituting compliance.

headings.title: Adherence to effective filings and 1972 continuation
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits issuing policies except pursuant to effective filings (subject to subsection 6) and continues rates and systems in effect on August 13, 1972, until withdrawn.

headings.title: Consent to excess rate on specific risk
headings.reviewNote: Permits using a rate in excess of an applicable filing on a specific risk upon the insured's written application stating reasons filed with the insurer.

headings.title: Rating organization filing authorization and withdrawal
headings.reviewNote: Deems rating organization members and subscribers to authorize director acceptance of organization filings, while detailing subscriber withdrawal, independent or agency filings, and approved member-rule procedures.

headings.title: Director review of changes within first six months
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to approve or disapprove any change to a filing during its first six months within ten days after receiving notice of the proposed change.

headings.title: Commercial property and casualty filing rules and notices
headings.reviewNote: Sets distinct commercial property and casualty rules: ten-day informational filings, rate/rule exemptions, $100,000+ form exemptions, five excluded lines, exemption notices (source note: 'subdivisions' in original rolls), sixty/thirty-day 25%+ renewal increase notices, ten-day coverage-restriction notices, definitions, and January 1, 2019 applicability.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates the definition, licensing, governance, non-discriminatory subscribership, and auditing services of insurance rating organizations.

headings.title: Definition and purpose of rating organization
headings.reviewNote: Defines rating organizations as entities that make and file rates, rating plans, rules, or audit insurance policies for members.

headings.title: Application for rating organization license
headings.reviewNote: Requires rating organizations to apply to the director, filing articles, bylaws, member lists, and resident service agent appointments.

headings.title: Licensing qualifications and triennial renewal
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes three-year licenses for qualified rating organizations upon payment of a twenty-five dollar fee, requiring prompt notices of changes.

headings.title: Non-discriminatory subscribership and service rules
headings.reviewNote: Requires rating organizations to admit insurers as subscribers without discrimination, providing regulatory review for rejected applicants.

headings.title: Prohibited rules restricting insurer dividends
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits rating organization rules that restrict payment of dividends, savings, or unabsorbed premium deposits to policyholders.

headings.title: Cooperation among rating organizations authorized
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes cooperation among rating organizations in ratemaking, subject to director review for unfair or unreasonable practices.

headings.title: Purchase of actuarial technical or other services
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any rating organization to subscribe for or purchase actuarial, technical, or other services, to be made available to all members and subscribers without discrimination.

headings.title: Definition of member of a rating organization
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'member of a rating organization' as an insurer entitled to participate in its management and electing to exercise that right.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes rating organization members and subscribers to file deviations, sets effective dates and termination rules, and opens deviation filings to public inspection.

headings.title: Filing of deviations from rating organization filings
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any member or subscriber of a rating organization to file a deviation from organization rates, schedules, plans, systems, or rules specifying its nature and extent.

headings.title: Effective date duration and termination of deviations
headings.reviewNote: Makes deviations effective upon delivery or registered mailing, continuing until terminated by filer notice or by the director after notice and hearing under section 379.323, unaffected by underlying changes without insurer consent.

headings.title: Public inspection and copies of deviation filings
headings.reviewNote: Opens deviation filings to public inspection upon being stamped filed within a reasonable time after receipt and allows copies upon payment of a reasonable charge; source note indicates word 'with' appears in original rolls.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines advisory organizations, establishes filing requirements, and empowers the director to order discontinuance of unfair practices.

headings.title: Definition of advisory organization
headings.reviewNote: Defines an advisory organization as any insurer group or association assisting insurers or rating organizations with loss/expense statistics or recommendations without making statutory filings.

headings.title: Required organizational filings by advisory organizations
headings.reviewNote: Requires advisory organizations to file their constitution, articles, bylaws, member list, resident process service agent, and examination agreement under section 379.343 with the director.

headings.title: Director hearings on unfair advisory practices
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the director to hold hearings if advisory organization practices or recommendations are unfair, unreasonable, or unlawful.

headings.title: Prohibited insurer reliance on noncompliant organizations
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits insurers from utilizing statistics or recommendations of advisory organizations that fail to comply with filing or discontinuance orders.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates joint underwriting and joint reinsurance groups, authorizing hearings and administrative orders against unfair practices.

headings.title: Joint underwriting and joint reinsurance groups
headings.reviewNote: Applies statutory regulation to groups, associations, or insurers engaging in joint underwriting or joint reinsurance operations.

headings.title: Administrative hearings and discontinuance orders
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the director, after a hearing, to issue a written order specifying and requiring discontinuance of any unfair, unreasonable, or statutorily inconsistent joint underwriting or joint reinsurance practice.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates quadrennial and discretionary examinations of insurers, rating, advisory, and joint organizations, governs oaths, costs, review and public filing of reports, and out-of-state report acceptance.

headings.title: Quadrennial and discretionary examinations of insurers and organizations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to examine subject insurers, rating organizations, advisory organizations, and joint groups at any time and requires an examination at least once every four years.

headings.title: Concurrent insurer examination under other state laws
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an insurer examination under this section may be made during an examination under other state laws.

headings.title: Production of books records and officer testimony
headings.reviewNote: Requires officers, managers, and agents to produce all books, accounts, and records for examination under oath.

headings.title: Payment of reasonable examination costs by examined entity
headings.reviewNote: Directs that the reasonable cost of any examination under this section be paid by the insurer, rating organization, advisory organization, or group examined.

headings.title: Review comment and public filing of examination reports
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits making an examination report public until the examined organization has an opportunity to review and file comments, after which the report and comments are filed for public inspection as admissible public records.

headings.title: Acceptance of out-of-state examination reports
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to accept an examination report made by another state's insurance supervisory official in lieu of an examination under this section.

entries.reviewSummary: States the compliance-verification purpose of examinations, requires public hearings on ten days' notice for suspected noncompliance, and mandates prohibition or compliance orders after hearing.

headings.title: Purpose of statutory compliance examinations
headings.reviewNote: States that the purpose of examination under section 379.017 and sections 379.316 to 379.361 is to enable the director to ascertain statutory compliance.

headings.title: Public hearing and ten-day notice on noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to hold a public hearing upon at least ten days' mailed written notice if examination findings show a rate, rating plan, or organization fails to meet statutory standards.

headings.title: Prohibition and compliance orders after hearing
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director, upon good-cause findings after hearing, to issue an order prohibiting further use of a noncompliant rate/plan within a reasonable period or requiring a noncompliant organization to comply.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs promulgation of statistical reporting plans, authorizes interstate regulatory data exchanges, and grants administrative rulemaking powers.

headings.title: Statistical reporting rules and loss experience
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to promulgate statistical reporting rules and loss experience data compilation plans for insurers.

headings.title: Interstate exchange of rating data and systems
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to exchange statistical information and consult with insurance supervisory officials of other states.

headings.title: Adoption of administrative rules by director
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the director to make reasonable administrative rules and regulations necessary to enforce rating statutes.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits excessive premiums, rebates, and unstated inducements by insurers, producers, and insureds, while permitting disclosed incidental fees.

headings.title: Prohibition of premium rebates and unstated benefits
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits insurers, producers, and insureds from charging noncompliant premiums or offering, giving, or knowingly accepting rebates or unstated inducements, while preserving producer commissions and policyholder dividends or savings.

headings.title: Authorized incidental fees and written disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes insurers, producers, agents, or brokers to charge additional incidental fees for installments, late payments, reinstatements, or similar authorized services when disclosed in writing.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes administrative orders, license revocations, and civil court actions for violations of property and casualty rating statutes.

headings.title: Administrative enforcement orders and penalty levels
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to issue administrative cease and desist orders and classify rating violations as level two violations under section 374.049.

headings.title: Civil enforcement actions and judicial remedies
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the director to initiate civil actions for injunctions and civil penalties against persons violating rating laws.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes insurers and producers to offer loss mitigation products, risk education services, and promotional merchandise without violating anti-rebate laws.

headings.title: Permitted loss prevention products and risk services
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes insurers and producers to offer free, discounted, or market-value products or services intended to prevent loss, control risk, or educate.

headings.title: Promotional merchandise and commercial advertising gifts
headings.reviewNote: Permits producers and insurers to provide gifts, goods, or promotional merchandise containing advertising to policyholders and the public.

headings.title: Exemption from anti-rebate and form filing statutes
headings.reviewNote: Deems loss prevention products and promotional gifts compliant with anti-rebate laws and exempts them from policy form filings.

headings.title: Administrative rulemaking authority and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Grants the director authority to exempt additional value-added services from anti-rebate prohibitions under chapter 536 procedures.

entries.reviewSummary: Delineates the application of casualty, fidelity, and motor vehicle rating laws and specifies statutory commercial exemptions.

headings.title: Scope and exceptions for casualty rating laws
headings.reviewNote: Applies sections 379.420 to 379.510 to casualty, fidelity, surety, and motor vehicle insurance lines, exempting reinsurance, workers' compensation, and aircraft.

headings.title: Exemption of commercial casualty insurance policies
headings.reviewNote: Exempts commercial casualty insurance policies from statutory rating provisions to the extent permitted under section 379.321.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes licensed casualty insurers to act in concert regarding rates, policy forms, and underwriting rules, including cosurety and affiliate transactions.

headings.title: Insurer concerted action in casualty ratemaking
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes licensed casualty insurers to act in concert in ratemaking, form preparation, underwriting rules, and loss statistics.

headings.title: Concerted ratemaking for cosureties and affiliates
headings.reviewNote: Permits insurers to act in concert in ratemaking when executing fidelity or surety bonds through cosurety, reinsurance, or common control.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates licensing for casualty rating organizations and specifies organizational documents, subscriber lists, and resident agent filings.

headings.title: Mandatory licensing for casualty rating organizations
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any entity from acting as a casualty rating organization without applying for and securing a license from the director.

headings.title: Eligibility and application for rating licenses
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes domestic and foreign corporations, partnerships, or individuals to apply for casualty rating organization licenses.

headings.title: Required application exhibits and service agent
headings.reviewNote: Requires license applicants to file constitutions, bylaws, member lists, resident process agent appointments, and qualifications.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs casualty rating organization licensing qualifications, sixty-day determination deadlines, and indefinite license duration until revocation.

headings.title: Director evaluation and issuance of license
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to issue a rating license specifying authorized lines upon finding the applicant qualified, competent, and compliant.

headings.title: Administrative sixty-day deadline for application action
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to grant or deny rating license applications in whole or in part within sixty days of filing.

headings.title: Indefinite duration of rating organization license
headings.reviewNote: Provides that rating organization licenses issued under this section remain in effect until revoked as provided in sections 379.420 to 379.510.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines casualty advisory organizations, mandates organizational filings and prompt change notices with the director, and prohibits unfair or unreasonable practices.

headings.title: Definition and required filings of advisory organizations
headings.reviewNote: Defines casualty advisory organizations and requires filing their constitution, articles, bylaws, member list, resident process service agent, and section 379.475 examination agreement.

headings.title: Prompt notice of changes in advisory filings
headings.reviewNote: Requires advisory organizations to notify the director promptly of every change in governing documents, member/subscriber lists, and designated resident process agent.

headings.title: Prohibition on unfair or unreasonable practices
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any advisory group, association, or organization from engaging in any unfair or unreasonable practice in its activities.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires joint underwriting groups engaging through joint reinsurance to make organizational filings, report changes promptly, and refrain from unfair or unreasonable practices.

headings.title: Required filings by joint underwriting groups
headings.reviewNote: Requires groups engaging in joint underwriting through joint reinsurance to file their constitution, articles, bylaws, member list, resident process service agent, and section 379.475 examination agreement.

headings.title: Prompt notice of changes in group filings
headings.reviewNote: Requires joint underwriting groups to notify the director promptly of every change in governing documents, member/subscriber lists, and designated resident process agent.

headings.title: Prohibition on unfair or unreasonable practices
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any joint underwriting group, association, or organization from engaging in any unfair or unreasonable practice in its activities.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes interstate ratemaking data exchange and consultation, and permits director-approved insurer agreements on rate adherence and equitable risk apportionment.

headings.title: Interstate exchange of ratemaking data and consultation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes rating organizations and insurers to exchange information and experience data and consult on ratemaking with insurers and rating organizations in Missouri and other states.

headings.title: Director-approved agreements to adhere to rates
headings.reviewNote: Permits two or more insurers, with director approval, to agree to adhere to rates, rating plans, rating systems, underwriting practices, or uniform modifications for covered casualty classes.

headings.title: Approved agreements for equitable apportionment of residual risks
headings.reviewNote: Permits director-approved insurer agreements for equitable apportionment of insurance for eligible applicants unable to procure coverage through ordinary methods and reasonable rate modifications.

headings.title: Written submission and public interest review of agreements
headings.reviewNote: Requires submitting insurer agreements in writing with requested information so the director can determine statutory consistency and public interest.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes discretionary examinations of casualty insurers and rating groups, mandates triennial rating organization examinations, governs oaths and costs, and permits accepting out-of-state reports.

headings.title: Discretionary examination of insurers and rating groups
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the director at any time deemed advisable to examine subject insurers, licensed rating organizations, section 379.455 advisory organizations, and section 379.460 joint groups.

headings.title: Concurrent insurer examination under other state laws
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an insurer examination under this section may be conducted during an examination under other state laws.

headings.title: Triennial examination of licensed rating organizations
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to examine or cause to be examined every licensed casualty rating organization at least once every three years.

headings.title: Examination under oath and production of records
headings.reviewNote: Permits examining officers, managers, agents, and employees under oath and requires exhibiting books, records, accounts, documents, and operational agreements requested by the director.

headings.title: Payment of reasonable examination costs by examined entity
headings.reviewNote: Requires the examined insurer, rating organization, advisory organization, or group to pay the reasonable cost of the examination.

headings.title: Acceptance of out-of-state examination reports
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to accept an examination report made by another state's insurance supervisory official in lieu of an examination under this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes director hearings on noncompliant casualty rates or rating organization practices, notice standards, and discontinuance orders.

headings.title: Purpose of casualty rating compliance examinations
headings.reviewNote: States that the purpose of examination is to enable the director to ascertain whether there is compliance with sections 379.420 to 379.510.

headings.title: Public hearing and ten-day notice on noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to hold a public hearing upon at least ten days' mailed written notice if examination gives reason to believe a rate, rating plan, or organization is noncompliant.

headings.title: Prohibition and compliance orders after hearing
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director, upon good-cause findings after hearing, to issue an order prohibiting further use of a noncompliant rate/plan within a reasonable period or requiring a noncompliant organization to comply.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes license suspension or revocation for noncompliance with section 379.480 orders, requires written findings, and permits modification or reversal.

headings.title: License suspension or revocation for order noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to suspend or revoke the license of a rating organization or insurer for affected classes of insurance upon failure to comply with a lawful section 379.480 order.

headings.title: Written order stating findings required for penalties
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits imposing any penalty, suspension, or revocation under sections 379.420 to 379.510 except upon a written order of the director stating findings.

headings.title: Authority to modify rescind or reverse suspension
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that the director's power to suspend or revoke includes the power to modify, rescind, or reverse such suspension or revocation.

entries.reviewSummary: Exempts insurer dividends, savings, and unabsorbed premium deposits from casualty rating regulation and excludes dividend plans from rating systems.

headings.title: Exemption of policyholder dividends and savings from regulation
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that sections 379.420 to 379.510 do not prohibit or regulate payment of dividends, savings, or unabsorbed premium deposits to policyholders, members, or subscribers.

headings.title: Exclusion of dividend plans from rating systems
headings.reviewNote: Provides that no plan for paying dividends, savings, or unabsorbed premium deposits to policyholders, members, or subscribers shall be deemed a rating plan or system.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs thirty-day hearing requests on orders made without hearing, twenty-day hearing and fifteen-day decision deadlines, informal evidentiary rules, chapter 536 judicial review, and stays pending appeal.

headings.title: Thirty-day hearing request on orders without hearing
headings.reviewNote: Allows an insurer or rating organization aggrieved by a director order or decision made without a hearing to make a written hearing request within thirty days after notice.

headings.title: Twenty-day hearing deadline and ten-day written notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to hear the requesting party within twenty days after receiving the request and give at least ten days' written notice of time and place.

headings.title: Fifteen-day decision deadline and interim order suspension
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director within fifteen days after hearing to affirm, reverse, or modify the prior action with reasons, suspending the prior action's effective date pending hearing and decision.

headings.title: Informality of pleading and evidentiary rules at hearings
headings.reviewNote: Provides that nothing in sections 379.420 to 379.510 requires observing formal rules of pleading or evidence at any hearing.

headings.title: Judicial review of director orders and rules
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes judicial review of final orders, rules, or decisions of the director in accordance with chapter 536 administrative procedures.

headings.title: Stay of orders pending judicial review
headings.reviewNote: Governs the stay and effective date of director orders pending judicial review, providing that affirmed orders relate back to issuance.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes administrative orders, level two penalties under section 374.049, and civil court actions for violating casualty orders.

headings.title: Administrative enforcement orders and penalty levels
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to issue administrative cease and desist orders and classify violations as level two violations under section 374.049.

headings.title: Civil enforcement actions and judicial remedies
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the director to initiate civil actions in circuit court to enforce final orders and recover statutory civil penalties.

entries.reviewSummary: Sets additional articles of association requirements for stock and mutual companies extending corporate existence or reorganizing.

headings.title: Additional articles requirements for stock reorganizations
headings.reviewNote: Requires reorganizing stock companies to state capital stock, shares, paid amounts, and increase capital to statutory minimums.

headings.title: Additional articles requirements for mutual reorganizations
headings.reviewNote: Requires reorganizing mutual companies to list policyholders, premium note values, assessments, and maintain assets equal to new mutuals.

entries.reviewSummary: Prescribes voting procedures and majority assent standards for insurance corporate reorganizations, protecting dissenting member rights.

headings.title: Voting on corporate reorganization and charter extension
headings.reviewNote: Requires formal shareholder or policyholder voting on corporate reorganization, charter extension, capital increases, and new articles.

headings.title: Required majority assent and dissenting member rights
headings.reviewNote: Requires majority stock or policyholder assent for reorganization and secures equitable asset payouts for non-assenting members.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires execution and acknowledgment of reorganized articles of association, verification affidavits, and filing with the director.

headings.title: Acknowledgment of articles and verification affidavit
headings.reviewNote: Directs directors or stockholders to acknowledge adopted articles and requires officers to execute an affidavit detailing the meeting proceedings.

headings.title: Filing of declaration and articles with director
headings.reviewNote: Requires the board of directors to submit the meeting declaration and acknowledged articles to the director of insurance.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs board acceptance of reorganization certificates, filings with the secretary of state, fee payments, and notices of readiness.

headings.title: Acceptance resolution and filing with secretary
headings.reviewNote: Directs board acceptance and filing with the secretary of state, extending corporate existence upon certificate issuance.

headings.title: Payment of corporate organization filing fees
headings.reviewNote: Requires payment of statutory corporate incorporation fees to the director of revenue upon filing articles of association.

headings.title: Commencement of duties by new board of directors
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a newly designated board of directors enters upon their duties at the expiration of the original corporate charter.

headings.title: Conforming capital structure and notice of readiness
headings.reviewNote: Directs the board to conform stock and business to general insurance statutes and notify the director of readiness to operate.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs regulatory examination of reorganized insurance companies and delivery of operating certificates confirming corporate authority.

headings.title: Examination of reorganized company and certificate issuance
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to examine reorganized companies, verifying capital and assets before issuing a certificate to do business.

headings.title: Cessation of special privileges and corporate continuity
headings.reviewNote: Terminates inconsistent special charter privileges upon original charter expiration while continuing corporate existence, assets, members, policies, and obligations without creating a new corporation.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs newspaper publication of notice upon filing a dissenting-interest petition and governs court hearings, net asset valuation decrees, and optional referee appointment.

headings.title: Clerk publication of newspaper notice of petition
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court clerk, upon filing of the petition, to publish newspaper notice in the county (or next nearest county) stating the petition's nature and that judgment will be entered at the next term.

headings.title: Hearing valuation decree payment and optional referee
headings.reviewNote: Directs the court at the next term to hear evidence, ascertain dissenting stockholders or policyholders and their equitable net asset values, decree payment discharging claims, and optionally refer the matter to a referee.

entries.reviewSummary: Entitles non-assenting stockholders and policyholders to appear as defendants in valuation proceedings governed by civil practice laws.

headings.title: Right of dissenting stakeholders to appear as defendants
headings.reviewNote: Entitles any non-assenting stockholder, policyholder, or mutual-department policyholder at original charter termination to appear as a defendant and be heard in the proceeding.

headings.title: Governance of proceedings by civil practice laws
headings.reviewNote: Provides that proceedings in the cause shall conform as near as may be to laws regulating practice in civil cases.

entries.reviewSummary: Sets additional articles of association requirements for stock and mutual companies surrendering special charters and reorganizing under general insurance statutes.

headings.title: Additional articles requirements for stock companies
headings.reviewNote: Requires stock company articles to state capital stock, share count, and amount paid per share in addition to section 379.590, increasing capital to the general statutory minimum if less.

headings.title: Additional articles requirements for mutual companies
headings.reviewNote: Requires mutual company articles to state policyholder count, premium notes, face value, assessments paid, and itemized cash and assets, with aggregate assets meeting new mutual minimums.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires voting on charter surrender and reorganization propositions and mandates unanimous stockholder or policyholder assent for adoption.

headings.title: Voting on charter surrender and reorganization
headings.reviewNote: Directs voting at the designated time and place on charter surrender, adopting general insurance statutes, reorganization, stock increase if needed, and proposed articles.

headings.title: Unanimous assent requirement and plan continuation choice
headings.reviewNote: Requires assent of all outstanding stock, all mutual policyholders, or both for stock-and-mutual companies, and allows stock-and-mutual companies to continue one plan and discontinue the other.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires acknowledgment of adopted reorganization articles, officer verification affidavit of meeting proceedings, and filing with the director.

headings.title: Acknowledgment of articles and verified meeting declaration
headings.reviewNote: Permits directors, five stockholders, or five mutual policyholders to sign and acknowledge adopted articles, and requires meeting officers to execute a verified affidavit declaration of proceedings and votes.

headings.title: Filing of declaration and articles with director
headings.reviewNote: Requires delivering the declaration and articles of association to the board of directors for submission and filing with the director.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs director examination and business certificate issuance for reorganized special-charter companies, effects charter surrender, and preserves corporate continuity.

headings.title: Director examination and business authorization certificate
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director, upon finding proper reorganization, statutory assets and capital, and solvency, to deliver a certificate and authorization to do business under general insurance statutes.

headings.title: Surrender of charter and substitution of general statutes
headings.reviewNote: Deems the company's special charter surrendered upon certification, with the articles of association and general insurance statutes substituted in its place.

headings.title: Cessation of special privileges and corporate continuity
headings.reviewNote: Terminates inconsistent special charter privileges while continuing the company as the same corporation without affecting asset titles, membership, policies, or existing obligations.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes the exchange of reciprocal or interinsurance contracts across property and casualty lines, excluding life insurance.

headings.title: Authorization of reciprocal and interinsurance contracts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes individuals, partnerships, and corporations as subscribers to exchange assessable or nonassessable reciprocal or interinsurance contracts for property, liability, fidelity and surety, accident and health, and miscellaneous insurance (excluding life and annuities).

headings.title: Bar on mixing assessable and nonassessable contracts
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits subscribers from exchanging assessable and nonassessable contracts at the same time and requires assessable agreements to impose contingent liability of at least one premium deposit.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires reciprocal exchanges to appoint the director to receive service of process and specifies three-copy service and forwarding procedures.

headings.title: Service of process through director of insurance
headings.reviewNote: Requires reciprocal attorneys to file an instrument appointing the director of insurance to accept service of process for the exchange.

headings.title: Forwarding copy of process to attorney
headings.reviewNote: Requires serving three copies of process on the director, who files one copy, forwards one copy to the attorney, and returns one copy with admission of service.

entries.reviewSummary: Sets minimum surplus requirements to commence and continue single-class and multi-class reciprocal business, mandates liability claim reserves, authorizes certificate sanctions, and provides surplus phase-in schedules.

headings.title: Minimum surplus to commence single-class business
headings.reviewNote: Requires a reciprocal or interinsurance exchange commencing business in one subdivision of section 379.650(1) to hold at least $1.6 million surplus in cash or securities in addition to required reserves.

headings.title: Minimum surplus to commence multi-class business
headings.reviewNote: Requires a reciprocal or interinsurance exchange commencing business in more than one subdivision of section 379.650(1) to hold at least $2.4 million surplus in cash or securities in addition to required reserves.

headings.title: Ongoing surplus maintenance to continue new business
headings.reviewNote: Requires any reciprocal or interinsurance exchange to maintain the surplus required to commence business in order to continue writing new business.

headings.title: Claim reserve fund for liability and workers compensation
headings.reviewNote: Requires maintaining a claim or loss reserve in cash or securities sufficient to discharge all outstanding losses for employer's liability, public liability, workers' compensation, and automobile insurance.

headings.title: Certificate suspension or revocation for section violations
headings.reviewNote: Makes violation of any provision of this section by a reciprocal or interinsurance exchange grounds for suspension or revocation of its certificate of authority by the director.

headings.title: Multi-year surplus phase-in for existing single class reciprocals
headings.reviewNote: Provides a multi-year phase-in schedule through December 31, 1992 ($1.0M to $1.6M) for single-class exchanges licensed on July 1, 1987, that lacked $1.6 million surplus on December 31, 1986.

headings.title: Multi-year surplus phase-in for existing multi-class reciprocals
headings.reviewNote: Provides a multi-year phase-in schedule through December 31, 1992 ($1.8M to $2.4M) for multi-class exchanges licensed on July 1, 1987, that lacked $2.4 million surplus on December 31, 1986.

headings.title: Transition period for reclassified single-class exchanges
headings.reviewNote: Allows exchanges lawfully operating under single-class surplus before August 28, 1989, that became subject to multi-class surplus requirements afterward to continue under single-class standards until December 31, 1990.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires subscribers or attorneys to make up reserve deficiencies, regulates repayment of advances, and defines net premiums.

headings.title: Mandatory assessment to make up asset deficiencies
headings.reviewNote: Requires subscribers or their attorney-in-fact to make up any asset deficiency if reserve funds fall below statutory requirements.

headings.title: Deposit and repayment of contributed deficiency funds
headings.reviewNote: Regulates funds advanced to cover deficiencies, holding them for subscribers under director terms until returned to depositors.

headings.title: Definition of net premiums and advance deposits
headings.reviewNote: Defines net premiums or deposits as advance payments made by subscribers after deducting contractual expense allowances.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates annual financial condition reporting by reciprocal attorneys and authorizes regulatory examinations funded by the exchange.

headings.title: Annual financial condition report by attorney
headings.reviewNote: Requires reciprocal attorneys to file annual calendar-year financial reports detailing solvency, collections, losses paid, subscriber returns, and expenses without disclosing subscriber names and addresses.

headings.title: Examination of reciprocal exchanges and assessment of costs
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to examine reciprocal business affairs and assets at the attorney's office, assessing costs to the exchange.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates annual certificates of authority for reciprocal attorneys, provides suspension procedures, and sets July first renewal dates.

headings.title: Annual certificate of authority requirement for attorney
headings.reviewNote: Requires reciprocal attorneys to procure an annual certificate of authority from the director certifying statutory compliance and fee payments.

headings.title: Suspension or revocation of reciprocal certificate
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to suspend or revoke a reciprocal certificate of authority upon statutory breach after notice and hearing.

headings.title: Annual renewal date and continuation of authority
headings.reviewNote: Establishes July first as the annual renewal date and continues existing certificates in effect pending renewal determinations.

entries.reviewSummary: Exempts reciprocal exchanges from general insurance laws, establishes rule of construction, and lists specifically applicable chapters.

headings.title: Exemption from general insurance statutes
headings.reviewNote: Exempts reciprocal exchanges from general insurance statutes unless specifically made applicable, with reciprocal statutes controlling conflicts.

headings.title: Applicable statutory chapters and sections
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates specific statutory chapters and sections applicable to reciprocals, including tax, regulatory supervision, and casualty rating laws.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits unauthorized reciprocal exchanges, provides for temporary organization permits, and authorizes administrative and civil sanctions.

headings.title: Unlawful execution without certificate of authority
headings.reviewNote: Declares exchanging indemnity contracts or soliciting applications without statutory compliance unlawful, authorizing organizational permits.

headings.title: Administrative enforcement orders and penalty levels
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to issue cease and desist orders and designates violations as level one violations under section 374.049.

headings.title: Civil enforcement actions and judicial remedies
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to initiate civil court actions to enforce compliance and seek statutory remedies for unauthorized exchanges.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs FAIR Plan property inspection requests, director-approved inspection scope, inspection reports and photographs, inspector disclosures, and five-day report transmittal.

headings.title: Request for FAIR Plan property inspection
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes property owners, insurers, or producers to request property inspections from the inspection bureau without written formalities.

headings.title: Facility prescription of inspection manner and scope
headings.reviewNote: Directs that the manner and scope of program business inspections be prescribed by the facility with the approval of the director.

headings.title: Inspection report contents and representative photograph
headings.reviewNote: Requires an inspection report for each inspected property covering structural and occupancy features and general building and surrounding conditions, and permits taking a representative photograph.

headings.title: Inspector disclosure of condition charges and coverage bar
headings.reviewNote: Requires the inspector to point out structural and occupancy features that may result in condition charges while barring the inspector from advising whether the facility will provide coverage.

headings.title: Submission of report to facility and applicant
headings.reviewNote: Directs prompt transmittal of inspection reports to the facility and makes copies available to property owners upon request.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs FAIR Plan policy issuance for eligible risks, apportionment of liability and expense assessments under section 379.835, and maximum location coverage limits.

headings.title: Policy issuance upon finding property eligible
headings.reviewNote: Directs the facility to issue a policy upon receiving an application and inspection report and finding the property eligible under the program.

headings.title: Apportionment of assumed liability to insurers
headings.reviewNote: Directs the facility to apportion assumed policy liability to participating insurers as provided in section 379.835.

headings.title: Governing committee expense assessments on insurers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the governing committee to levy program expense assessments on participating insurers under section 379.835 subject to committee minimum assessments.

headings.title: Maximum liability limits per habitational or commercial location
headings.reviewNote: Caps program liability at $200,000 for habitational property and $1,000,000 for commercial property at one location, directs placement assistance for excess requests, and defines 'location'.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines sinkhole loss, authorizes supplemental FAIR Plan sinkhole policies for habitational structures beginning January 1, 2015, and allows expedited approval and investigation procedures.

headings.title: Definition of sinkhole loss and required evidence
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'sinkhole loss' as physical damage from sudden earth settlement or collapse caused by subterranean limestone or similar rock voids evidenced by four enumerated structural and condemnation criteria.

headings.title: Supplemental habitational sinkhole loss policies and exclusions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the plan, beginning January 1, 2015, to issue supplemental habitational sinkhole-loss policies, excluding driveways, nonhabitational detached structures, land value, and sinkhole filling costs, with contents covered only upon structure loss.

headings.title: Applicable statutes risk-based premiums and claims investigation
headings.reviewNote: Applies sections 379.810 to 379.880 (source note: word 'section' appears in original rolls), permits expedited approval and sinkhole-risk-only premiums, and authorizes specific claims investigation procedures.

entries.reviewSummary: Prescribes five-day FAIR Plan action reports, underwriting standards, policy issuance and producer commissions, conditional improvement reinspections, surcharges, and appeal notices.

headings.title: Five-day facility action report and risk determinations
headings.reviewNote: Requires the facility within five business days of receiving an inspection report and application to complete an action report stating whether the risk is acceptable, surcharged, conditionally acceptable upon improvements, or unacceptable.

headings.title: Reasonable underwriting standards and prohibited declination criteria
headings.reviewNote: Requires declination notice when failing reasonable underwriting standards (physical condition and use/housekeeping), while barring neighborhood location or uncontrolled environmental hazards as declination criteria.

headings.title: Acceptance notice policy issuance and producer commission
headings.reviewNote: Directs notifying the applicant and designated licensed producer of acceptability and premium, issuing the policy within three business days of premium receipt effective at 12:00 noon, and paying producer commission.

headings.title: Conditional declination improvement notice and reinspection
headings.reviewNote: Requires promptly advising applicants of needed improvements upon conditional declination and promptly reinspecting and processing the application once improvements are completed.

headings.title: Substandard condition surcharges under approved filings
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes imposing surcharges for substandard conditions revealed by inspection in conformity with director-approved filings.

headings.title: Report transmittal and appeal notice upon declination
headings.reviewNote: Requires promptly sending inspection and action reports to the property owner and director upon declination or conditional acceptance, with written notice of section 379.850 appeal rights and procedures.

entries.reviewSummary: Creates the Joint Reinsurance Association to assume 100% reinsurance from the FAIR Plan facility, apportions habitational and commercial shares, and requires director approval of its plan of operation.

headings.title: Creation of Joint Reinsurance Association and reinsurance
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Joint Reinsurance Association of all insurers to assume 100% reinsurance from the facility and distribute liability under section 379.825.

headings.title: Proportional insurer participation by habitational and commercial lines
headings.reviewNote: Apportions each insurer's participation in writings, expenses, profits, and losses proportionally by its habitational premiums written and commercial premiums written.

headings.title: Director approval of plan of operation and rules
headings.reviewNote: Requires the association to file its plan of operation, rules of procedure, and any amendments with the director for approval before taking effect.

entries.reviewSummary: Restricts FAIR Plan policy cancellation grounds, mandates thirty days' advance notice with reasons, and requires inspection and appeal disclosures.

headings.title: Restricted grounds for policy or binder cancellation
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits cancelling a FAIR Plan policy or binder without governing committee approval except for evidence of incendiarism, nonpayment of premium, fraud or material misrepresentation, or changed conditions rendering the risk uninsurable.

headings.title: Thirty-day advance notice and statement of reasons
headings.reviewNote: Requires sending notice of cancellation or nonrenewal with a statement of reasons to the insured at least thirty days in advance while retaining a copy.

headings.title: Inspection procedures and appeal right disclosure in notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires cancellation or nonrenewal notices to include inspection request procedures and a statement of the insured's right of appeal.

entries.reviewSummary: Grants applicants a thirty-day direct appeal to the director on coverage acceptance conditions and provides governing committee appeals reviewable by the director.

headings.title: Direct applicant appeal to director on acceptance conditions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any applicant to appeal a facility decision regarding conditions for acceptance of coverage in writing to the director within thirty days.

headings.title: Appeals to governing committee and further appeal to director
headings.reviewNote: Grants applicants and insurers a right to appeal other decisions to the governing committee, whose decision may be appealed in writing to the director within thirty days.

entries.reviewSummary: Sets FAIR Plan producer commission rates for new and renewal business and directs undesignated commissions to a federal riot-reinsurance fund or general revenue.

headings.title: Producer commission rates on new and renewal business
headings.reviewNote: Sets program commissions at twelve percent on new business and ten percent on renewal business of the policy premium, payable to the designated licensed producer.

headings.title: Disposition of commissions when no producer is designated
headings.reviewNote: Directs depositing undesignated commissions into a director-held fund for Missouri's contribution under U.S. Public Law 90-448, with unapplied funds paid to general revenue one year after program termination.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates the structure, member appointments, terms, vacancies, and personal immunity of the FAIR Plan governing committee.

headings.title: Program administration by governing committee and manager
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the FAIR Plan program is administered by a facility governing committee under director supervision and operated by a committee-appointed manager.

headings.title: Thirteen-member committee composition and group limit
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a thirteen-member governing committee (ten elected under the plan of operation and three director-appointed: one Missouri insurer and two licensed agents), limiting each insurer group to one seat.

headings.title: Interim director appointments to fill committee vacancies
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to appoint a representative to fill any governing committee vacancy pending designation or election under the program.

headings.title: Immunity from liability for committee acts
headings.reviewNote: Confers immunity from personal civil liability on governing committee members, officers, and employees for official acts in good faith.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs annual and special meetings of FAIR Plan insurers and the governing committee, twenty-day notices, quorums, mail voting, and two-thirds weighted voting.

headings.title: Annual meeting of insurers and governing committee
headings.reviewNote: Requires an annual meeting of participating insurers and governing committee members on a date fixed by the committee.

headings.title: Calling of special meetings by committee or insurers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes calling a special meeting by the committee or upon written request of any ten insurers, with no more than one from the same management or ownership group.

headings.title: Meeting notice agenda quorum and proxy voting
headings.reviewNote: Requires twenty days' written notice with an agenda, sets a majority of insurers as a quorum, and permits voting by proxy.

headings.title: Unanimous committee authorization for mail voting
headings.reviewNote: Permits proposing and voting on matters by mail if unanimously authorized by committee members present and voting, with at least twenty days' mailed notice.

headings.title: Weighted insurer voting and two-thirds approval threshold
headings.reviewNote: Directs casting and counting insurer votes on a weighted basis by premiums written (or habitational/commercial premiums for exclusive proposals), requiring two-thirds of weighted votes cast for approval.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs meeting schedules, manager appointments, annual budgeting, reporting duties, quorums, and underwriting committees.

headings.title: Regular meetings of the governing committee
headings.reviewNote: Directs the governing committee to meet as often as necessary to administer the program or upon call of the director.

headings.title: Appointment of program manager and staff compensation
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the committee to appoint a program manager, determine compensation, and establish employee benefit programs.

headings.title: Annual operating budget preparation by manager
headings.reviewNote: Directs the manager to prepare an annual operating budget for committee approval and transmission to participating insurers.

headings.title: Annual report of operations to director and insurers
headings.reviewNote: Mandates furnishing an annual written operational and financial report to participating insurers and the director.

headings.title: Quorum requirements for governing committee action
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that the presence of seven members, including at least five insurers, constitutes an official quorum for committee action.

headings.title: Appointment of underwriting and specialized committees
headings.reviewNote: Directs the appointment of an underwriting committee and authorizes additional specialized committees as deemed advisable.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates separate statistical recordkeeping and annual reporting on FAIR Plan inspections, policies, declinations, and approvals.

headings.title: Statistical coding and program data maintenance
headings.reviewNote: Requires the facility to separately code and maintain distinct statistical records of business written under the FAIR Plan.

headings.title: Annual statistical report to director and HUD
headings.reviewNote: Requires the manager to submit annual statistical reports to the committee, director, and HUD detailing inspections and policies.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires sixty days' advance notice with specific factual grounds for commercial casualty cancellations and nonrenewals, exempting affiliate transfers.

headings.title: Sixty-day notice requirement for commercial cancellations
headings.reviewNote: Requires sixty days' advance written notice for commercial casualty cancellations, exempting nonpayment, fraud, increased hazard, or insolvency.

headings.title: Sixty-day notice requirement for commercial nonrenewal
headings.reviewNote: Mandates sixty days' advance written notice mailed or delivered to the named insured before nonrenewal of commercial casualty policies.

headings.title: Statement of actual reason and affiliate transfer exemption
headings.reviewNote: Requires specific factual reasons for cancellation or nonrenewal and exempts inter-affiliate transfers from nonrenewal notice rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines commercial casualty rating terms, regulates scheduled rating debits and credits, and mandates written explanations for factor changes.

headings.title: Definitions for commercial casualty rating provisions
headings.reviewNote: Defines A-rated risk, base rate, classification, classification system, commercial casualty insurance, director, rate, rating plan, and rating system.

headings.title: Inapplicability to hazard exposure and A-rated adjustments
headings.reviewNote: Exempts rate adjustments resulting from changes in operating hazard, payroll or sales exposure changes, and judgment-based A-rated risks.

headings.title: Scheduled rating notice and written explanation rights
headings.reviewNote: Requires notice on policy renewals of premium increases due to scheduled rating factor changes and mandates written explanations upon request.

headings.title: Premium alteration notice requirements for commercial renewals
headings.reviewNote: Directs that commercial casualty renewals involving significant premium increases follow section 379.321 premium alteration notification rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates annual March first closed commercial casualty claims reports, including large noneconomic and punitive verdict counts, while excluding section 374.415 and chapter 383 reports.

headings.title: Annual report of closed commercial casualty claims
headings.reviewNote: Requires commercial casualty insurers to file annual March first closed-claims reports covering profitability by line, claims closed with and without payment and reserves by year incurred, and court-verdict counts exceeding $300,000 and $500,000 in noneconomic or punitive damages.

headings.title: Exclusion of section 374.415 and chapter 383 data
headings.reviewNote: Excludes information already reported to the director under section 374.415 or any provision of chapter 383 from the annual report required by this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines prepaid legal service plans, establishes statutory exemptions, and mandates written consumer disclosures that plans are not insurance.

headings.title: Definition of prepaid legal service plan
headings.reviewNote: Defines prepaid legal service plans collecting periodic fees, exempting individual retainers, indigent aid, ERISA plans, and union programs.

headings.title: Mandatory consumer disclosure for prepaid legal plans
headings.reviewNote: Requires membership solicitors to provide written disclosures that prepaid legal plans are not insurance and not regulated by the department.
